He’d been assigned to the task of looking over and diagnosing the health of the economy, and had been given access to several classified League files to accomplish this task. Abrasha thought to himself that perhaps an increase in responsibilities was on the horizon.

Eleven hours later, the once tidy looking man in uniform was now an out of control mess, with sweat dripping down his face as the temperature had gotten to a point where he had thrown his jacket to the floor. On that floor now lay countless papers and charts, painting a terrifying picture that only those with the proper knowledge could decrypt.

He slowly sank to a sitting position, sliding down the wall as he did so. Abrasha now truly understood it all. Russia no longer had an economy. In its place an engine had been constructed. That engine used the scraps of what was once prosperity to fuel a complete and total war without any chance of returning to normalcy after. Only now could he truly understand where Russia was heading, swallowed whole into the dark abyss of hatred.

options.name: “What have they done to the motherland?”

title: On Minefields
desc:
“There are no minefields in Russia and they were told to keep it that way.

Officially, the Black League espouses the need for prisoners of war to 'tame the motherland' by fertilizing the soil for farms, flattening the earth for infrastructure and urban development as well digging holes with which to bury the dead and further fortify the state.

Truth was that Leonid and his group of young prisoners had the unenviable task of clearing the land of mines that the several russian warlords had laid all throughout their motherland. Sometimes it was as easy as following the map that detailed the minefield. Other times it was as hard as finding needles in a haystack.

Clearing the mines was made harder by the fact that each of them had been given selective treatment depending on which warlord they served along with what other 'war crimes' they may have committed. If they had served a naive but benevolent warlord on top of being a 'good servant of the motherland', then they were allowed tools and a single slice of bread a day. Being the opposite meant having nothing or being executed by minefield.

He hoped that one day he and his fellow prisoner would be free men. But until the last of the teutons are dead and until justice has been served, they shall never be free."[Change Later]

title: The Men On The Front
desc:
Late into yet another Siberian night, Andrei reclined back in his chair with a newspaper and vodka in each of his hands, having missed the chance to read it earlier in the day. In large, bold letters, the headline read, “GERMANY THREATENS NUCLEAR WAR”. At the bottom corner of that same page was a public service announcement from the government, informing the public of how those first allowed into the National Redoubt System would be members of the army and their families, followed by the general populace.

Andrei himself had a mixture of emotions swirling through his head. On one hand, he, his wife, and children were guaranteed a spot after having been working in the League's governmental apparatus since before the Reunification Wars. But, besides the potential for the very collapse of humanity itself, Andrei pondered the fate of the millions of his Russian comrades who wouldn’t make it into the bunkers. Would they just be tossed aside? Discarded as though they were only a means to an end? The conclusion of that last thought was enough to convince Andrei that he needed to just go to bed, simply forget these thoughts and return to work at the recruitment office without such things to ponder.

The next morning brought something he’d never seen before. Usually, a recruitment office is almost always empty, and with little activity in it, and Andrei had worked in this building for over a decade, and his team never had an amount of enlistment requests that came close to challenging.

But that morning when he went to open the doors to the building, he saw a line of people that had to have been miles long. Andrei saw the terrified faces of tens of thousands, no doubt having read the same words and had the same thoughts he had the night before.

That day, Andrei helped thousands of families obtain spots in the bunkers, with ever more pleading and begging to have their fathers and husbands enlist so that they too may avoid the worst fate imaginable. Yet, as more and more pleaded and begged to enlist, Andrei knew he could only save so many before the military blocked any further enlistment.

options.name: Vengeance demands the highest of prices.

title: A Pain Beyond Pain
desc:
Major Friedrich Schäfer sat, handcuffed to a chair, beaten and bloodied. Dozens of cuts oozed across his body. They'd torn out his fingernails on the third day, and blood stained his once pristine uniform. The interrogation room was ice cold, every surface formed of featureless grey brick. The only sound was the humming of the lights over head.

The door to his prison slammed open, and struck the wall with a bang. Two men of the Black League, both part of the reborn interrogation cadres, shuffled inside. Behind them, a new man took the stage.

He was tall, so tall that he had to duck beneath the lip of the door. He was bald, and wore a white lab coat. His arms were inhumanely long, stretched thin like taffy, and a syringe of amber liquid sloshed in his black-gloved hands. "Ah, here is the patient." One of the interrogators offered him a stool next to Schäfer's immobilized body. "Thank you for your patience," the doctor said, smiling. He took the offered seat. "I do hope my friends have not been too brutal to you. Sometimes, I think they act in such a manner because they're simply bored." His smile dimmed. "Or perhaps they saw what happened in Smolensk."

Friedrich spat a foul mixture of blood and spit at the doctor's face. "Kill me now, untermensch. I will tell you nothing."

"That is your choice, my friend. But, I would like to test that hypothesis." The doctor gripped Schäfer's arm, and pierced the closest of his bulging veins without another word. The amber medicine poured into his body in seconds.

Every nerve in the Major's body ignited. He seized, foam bubbling in his mouth as he threw himself back and forth, unable to control his own movements. The legs of his chair slipped from the ground. Friedrich screamed as his skull cracked against the concrete floor. His lungs strained, and his heart felt as though it was soon to burst. "Please!" he screamed, "I'll talk! I'll talk!"

"No, my friend," the doctor said.

options.name: [Change Later]"I'm getting wonderful data from this."[Change Later]

title: Free Loaders
desc:
[Change Later]"Please! It's not for us, it's just for the baby! Pleeease!

Yuri's hands tightened around the rough kitchen counter, growing whiter with every cry of desperation from his sobbing wife. A whole year they had been 'living' in this soulless concrete shell. A year since they had had every family photo, every rug and ring, every ounce of color mercilessly stripped from them, sent into the belly of the foul factories. A year he had been forced to feed them, put screw upon miserable screw into radios he could never play, first aid kits he could never use.

"Pleeeeeease! Just take half! Leave us with some! Our baby is all we have!"

But they had kept going, like reeds floating in rapids, trying their damndest not to snap. And it had paid off. The miracle of life. The League could not snuff out the joy that a parent felt as a child, their child, grew. But they were trying their best. For the crime of possessing some simple wooden blocks and and some meager rations, they had sent two of the League's lackeys; a snivelly but ferocious boy, his hat too big for his head, and a towering giant of a man, his eyes two sharpened daggers. A duo as comical as it was terrifying.

But Yuri didn't care. This would be his stand. The knife in the drawer beneath his hand was bent and blunted, but it stabbed all the same. He would show everyone what good Russian people did to those who crossed the line. He'd wipe that stupid smug face off this baron in black. He would -

Angela crumpled to the floor, her arms clutching her bloodied and mutilated belly, her face now a reflection of Yuri's soul: pale and panic-stricken.

"There! Now you really don't need these little blocks and extra calories."

With a pleased smile, the two devils in uniform exited through the door, the baron giving Yuri one more crushing glare. A glare of pity, as if he was a fool to think he had ever had any control of the situation. A glare of victory.

And then the room was silent again. The frantic cries of Angela, replaced by quiet, uncanny sobs. The rage that had filled Yuri's soul, now crushed, ground into dust, and scattered before the cold midnight wind. And the beating heart of his unborn child, silenced. They would now never gaze upon all the colors and lights and sounds and smells of the world.

But perhaps that was for the best.

options.name: For the reclamation of Russia, no sacrifice is too great.

title: Separate the Wheat from the Chaff
desc:
A knock rang out from a humble house on the outskirts of Barnaul, a major grain producing area within the [OMS.GetName]. A rude awakening was to await its owner, who was ready to sell his grain the next day.

"Comrade Nikita, your grain has been deemed unsuitable for the general populace. It is too expensive and decadent for the people of the Great Trial."

Nikita shook life a leaf; this nameless official had condemned his harvest, and therefore his life. Panicking, Nikita cried out. "B-but you can’t do that, that's the entire stockpile for the year! How am I supposed to buy rations from the storage? I'll starve! You aren't so cruel, are you?"

Nikita stared at the officer, hoping that just this once, the Spartan discipline of the Black League would be relaxed for him, just this once. The officer's eyes wavered a tiny bit. Maybe they'd give him the standard pricing, even if they didn't agree to his asked prices. How dare they, anyhow? After the Union collapsed, he built his own way, he made his estate in Barnaul!

The officer slowly shook his head, "Sir, one farmer's life doesn’t matter in the grand scheme of the nation. If you starve, you shall be replaced with another, more capable person. We will begin the confiscation of this improper yield. Please vacate the field, or you will be arrested for treason."

The officer shook his head, looking away from the grim situation. For a moment, he faltered. His mind thought of traitorous things. What right did they have to kill this man for a mistake? They could just call it mass-produced, it'd be a simple response for a simple mistake. What was the point in a government to reclaim Russia if they were going to destroy their own people?

His train of thought was rudely interrupted by farmer Nikita, now on his knees, crying and begging for another chance. "I'll plant the crops, it doesn't matter to me! Just enough to live!" The last thing the officer said in the confrontation was a simple, harsh...

title: More For The Soldiers
desc:
Even through some of the harshest training programs that existed in the world, not once had Mizenov ever felt like the League had not given him enough. Meals, a roof over his head, and even a degree of respect he hadn’t ever been given before in his life were some of the things that enlisting in the military had helped him obtain.

And it didn’t stop there. Many of the civilian encounters he had often ended in a salute for his eventual service in The Great Trial, or an acknowledgement of his bravery. It had always made him even more proud to be a part of the cause, yet something always seemed a little lost in their eyes.

Mizenov never quite knew why. At least until his unit passed by the village of his childhood.

As his transport vehicle bumped along the road, he turned his gaze to the buildings he used to sleep under as a child. Although he remembered the structures never being in the best of shape, they certainly never reached the state they were in now. Pieces of brick were missing all throughout it, with many of the windows being boarded over.

And it was then that he saw the occupants of the village. Each and every one looked as though they hadn’t been fed in at least a week, with plenty of bones remaining visible. Upon their faces sat the looks of despair that Mizenov hadn’t seen since the days of the terror bombings, in some cases some even looked to have drifted into an even darker place...

The sight of his fellow Russians in such a state almost brought tears to his eyes, as this scene repeated again and again as the convoy passed through even more of the countryside. Village after village, turning men and women into fuel for the engine of war. It was the only time in his life where the seeds of doubt grew into a deep, underlying anger at the League. Perhaps, he thought, that maybe Russia had a deeper, much darker enemy than the Aryan.

options.name: “The price for vengeance is never too high.”

title: The Men in the Factories
desc:
“Listen up!”

A certainly strange awakening, unlike the usual inhumane conditions they usually live in. Dominik was certain that it wouldn’t be much more special than another word about increased quotas or a small promotion, it had never been special before, why would it today. At the factory in Barnaul, there was always a collective pessimism between the workers. They all knew that they would all one day fall to the cold embrace of death, they weren’t scared of it, the present couldn’t be much more different from it.

“Under the commandment of the central command of the All-Russian Black League, we will teach you how to survive a nuclear fallout which the Teutonic menace might one day wreak upon us. The closest fallout shelter lies to the room left of us, near the offices. If the sound of sirens rings out, please try to get to the shelter as soon as possible. If you are not quick enough, or you don’t have the time to get to your local fallout shelter, please stay calm and go as deep as you can in your building. Any other information will be detailed in the pamphlet you will receive, thank you.”

The soldiers around the officer handed out a pamphlet to every worker in the building. On the paper there were pictures showing a step by step guide on how to survive the nukes from the teutons. Dominik was surprised that they could be so compassionate, or perhaps they just wanted to have their cheap labor survive. In any case, it was a feeble attempt at giving the people hope. He doubted if most would even try to survive, he could try to, but would it be a happier life in a dead world. From the small things he had heard about this foreign ‘nuke’, it didn’t sound very pleasant to live in a world where it destroyed the world.

options.name: He lost the small hope they tried to give him.

title: Expand the Bunkers West
desc:
The deep rumbling of cement mixers and the roar of truck engines awoke Vadim from his short sleep. It had only been a week or so since the league had occupied his village, and he had sure as hell not enjoyed it. Starting at 6 o’clock every morning they would start construction around the hills surrounding the settlement, and stop around nine in the afternoon.  Working on what? He had absolutely no idea. The elders had gathered the community upon the arrival of the workers, instructing them to stay away and avoid the workers and the sites at all costs.

He was sick to death of them. Not a single night’s good sleep was had since those bastards had arrived! It was time to do something about it, even if there were some damn consequences. Leaving his house, making his way through the town square and hiking up the steep hill towards the main site, before moving through the bushes, peering into the scene below.

There were about 20 of them, the majority seeming to be workers of sorts. Looking starved and haggled, they were either lined up towards the officers inspecting them or slaving away at a large pit in the centre. Digging yet deeper into the earth, as they began lifting heavy concrete slabs and steel doors into the pit, Vadim only grew more puzzled. What just was going on here? The nearest town worth anything was Syktyvkar, and that was hundreds of miles away. What did his place matter? And what were they building? A shelter of sorts, maybe even a bunk-

He met the gaze of the officer staring at him, screaming while pointing directly at his face. There was no time to hear the shouts and orders they would give him if he stuck around another second. He just knew he had to run as fast as god would let him.

Dashing into his village, He caught his breath and started to make his way home and prayed they wouldn’t recognize him again.

title: Dig Deeper
desc:
At a table sat a group of engineers and architects, rolling out several schematics and plans that were to be the main talking point of this hastily assembled meeting. They were ordered by the League to gather together once more to discuss an extension of the same bunkers that they had all spent so much work on. Not that they could complain or say no to such an order, but it frustrated them all nonetheless.

Most frustrated of all was the designated leader of the group, Kolya, who quickly began to realize that a previously mildly aggravating situation had just developed into an unbelievably painful one, as it became clear to all present that such a request related to the expansion of underground bunker sites would require materials that their superiors simply did not have possession of.

They would need to find an alternative. Something cheaper, and in vast amounts so as to supply other sites with the means to pursue their own expansion operations if need be.

Then, they had it: Steel. It only had to be layered twice as thick as lead to get the same effectiveness, and it was 3 times as cheap. And if constructed in a fashion where the maximum amount of dirt possible could be in between the steel lining and potential radioactive fallout, the occupants of the bunker would be relatively safe.

But, the issue of effective air filtration would arise, as those too needed design changes according to the orders of the League.

Kolya and the group pondered this for a while, as they wondered how they could possibly downgrade air filtration without harming the occupants in the process. But they had to come to an answer at some point, and that involved simply hoping and praying that a few experimental methods would be enough.

But of course, they couldn’t tell their benefactors this, as the consequence for implementing plans with such blatant logical holes in them would be severe. So, with smiles and neutral faces, they later informed the council assigned to oversee them of their “successful discovery” of new design methods.

title: More Ears on the Border
desc:
It was supposed to be his off day, Braun thought as he rode by car back to his forward base near the Russian border. Torrential rains hammered on his car's windows. For some reason, the Generalfeldmarschall had called Braun to the front once again to deal with yet another inconsequential matter, probably for some slave revolts.

As soon as he reached the base, he looked at the map on the diminutive planning table. His heart froze when he saw the damning maps in front of him. Over the past weeks, the "Reclamation Government" had begun a massive buildup along the German frontier, and he had been oblivious to it? He knew the Russians had unified, but invading the Reich? It was absurd! More importantly, Braun shuddered to think about what it meant for his career.

An unexpected voice made him jump: his commanding officer. "Care to explain your negligence, Generalleutenant? You've been noticeably absent from your duties." the Generaloberst demanded.

"Herr Generaloberst, I was not under the impression that these were serious rep-" Braun stammered. Suddenly, his superior slammed the table in frustration, ripping the map with a gash where the German border was.

"Do you think this is a game?!" he roared in Braun's face. "We could be attacked at any moment, all for your laying about in Moskau! I need your plan, and I need you to get your ass out there to implement it right now!"

Braun had seen what those madmen did to his fellow pilot when he crash-landed in Omsk, in 1963, during the Anarchy. Had he condemned his people to not being prepared to fight against this rabid beast? What if they got into Moskau, or Sankt Petersburg, or beyond?

Ashamed and afraid, Braun spoke up. "I apologize, sir. Fortifications will be built along with the proposed conscription for all adults and emergency defense measures. Sieg Heil!"

Despite the bluster, Braun was nervous. While the Russians were a weaker people, while they didn't have the same economy, Braun knew that Yazov's Black League had one thing: hatred. All encompassing, brutal, murderous, grasping, hatred. Any tactic, any sacrifice, any idea, no matter how depraved or brutal, would be thrown at the noble German people to annihilate them.

title: Under Lock And Key
desc:
Marin closed his diary, sighing and looking out the window at the street below. As he did so, his thoughts ached at him. Thoughts of his dear lover, Sasha. He hadn’t been able to see her for a while, and the heartache he felt grew more prominent within his mind each and every day it continued.

He sat up straight, a plan forming in his mind. His eyes shot over to the clock, revealing that the 10 PM curfew would be in effect minutes from now. Marin began to pace around the room, running his hands through his hair as he considered his options. He could wait yet another night, which would probably be yet another sleepless one. So he decided to run the gauntlet, and finally see his dear lover and soulmate for the first time in months.

As he set his feet out on the pathway, he found the brightness of the moon above him both a blessing and a curse, as the first League patrols proceeded to begin the sweeping of the streets. Quietly moving behind whatever could pass for cover, he expertly maneuvered around easily a dozen patrols. Soon, he was only a block away from his dear Sasha. Smiling, he reveled in his progress so far. And it was then that he tripped, letting out a blood curdling scream into the darkness.

He immediately stood up, knowing exactly what was coming for him. Marin could only put faith into his speed, as the flashlights of patrols bounced off of the walls in front of him, soon accompanied by the terrifying sounds of gunshots. But, he did have a lead on the soldiers, and he turned the final corner, almost at the finish line. Sasha's apartment couldn’t have been more than a hundred feet away.

But...something started to burn in his back...he grew weak, losing all strength in his legs as he fell into a pool of blood. Through ever darkening vision, he saw the horrified face of his lover, who had opened her window to see where the noises were coming from. As the two locked eyes, Marin summoned one last bit of strength. He died with a smile on his lips, as his final thoughts only contained love and happiness.

options.name: The last candles of hope in Russia are being snuffed out.

title: Fortresses Among The Tundra
desc:
Andrei joined the Black League to avenge the family he’d lost in the Second Trial. To reclaim Moscow. To destroy the Teuton, once and for all. Digging a trench on the steppes of European Russia was a far cry from that. He was in an endless cycle: he'd wake up, eat breakfast, dig, eat lunch, dig more, eat dinner, dig even more, then go to sleep. It didn’t help that the ground had almost frozen solid from the weather. On top of that, it was supposed to rain the next day. Chances were, the dirt would turn to mud and undo much of their progress. It didn't matter, in Andrei's eyes. They'd been digging in the same damn spot for three weeks now and had nothing to show for it.

Once again, he plunged his shovel into the earth ahead of him once more, only to be met with a clang. He tried the same spot again a couple times, the same result producing itself each time. "Why have you stopped digging," the commissar overseeing the men demanded. "It’s the soil, sir," Andrei replied, "It’s frozen solid!"

"Then dig faster! Harder! Use your hands if you have to!"

“If you want this done faster, maybe grab your own fucking shovel and get digging,” a soldier cried. The commissar’s head snapped to the source of the demand, and he motioned with his hand for one of his guards to grab the man and bring him before him.

"What is your name, soldier?" the commissar growled. Rather than being cowed, the young soldier spit a phlegmy blob right onto the commissar's eye. The camp froze for one moment. The commissar dazedly wiped his face with a leather-bound hand.

Silently, slowly, the commissar drew his service pistol from its holster. For a split second, one could see the private attempt to struggle fruitlessly before the commissar fired a single round into his skull. His body slumped backwards into the trench. "When that bell rings, you will ignore it and keep digging," the commissar ordered.

The next morning it was raining, and as Andrei predicted, their work had been washed away.

options.name: And the private's body was never found.

title: The T.V’s will Run Black
desc:
Yustina Novikova was doing her usual business in her family’s household, a small bungalow outside of Krasnoyarsk. She lived with her family of four, her two daughters Marianna and Lana, her husband Adrik and finally herself. All in all, they were lucky. Adrik was not in the front, and yet they survived, working at the local artillery factory. As she was finishing her chores for the day, Lana ran up to her. Lana was a very artistic child and she often showed her art to her mother. This day she had made a rather terrifying piece.

The drawing looked like a demon with a German helmet languishing in pain while it burned upon a stake of fire. Around the stake were multiple people cheering as the Teuton burned. The drawing was comically unrealistic and simple, yet disturbing to look at. Yustina carefully handed the drawing back to Lana.

"See? It’s a German burning, like teacher said they should! I saw it on T.V! I hate the evil Teutons!" Lana shouted in childish rage. Yustina couldn't muster much of a response to her outbursts — they terrified her. "Do you also hate them, mommy?"

"Well, Lana... hate is a scary thing. Very scary." she offered.

Lana frowned. "But Mommy, school says that hating the enemy is good. And the 'clab-rat-ors' sold us out!"

"I just think you shouldn't draw these things, honey." Yustina sighed.

Lana frowned and crumpled the drawing in her round little hands. "Well, I'll tell the teacher you won't let me!"

Yustina grabbed Lana by the shoulder before she could scamper off. "You will do no such thing! You'll do as I say! Throw that drawing away, and don't you dare tell the teacher, or you won't have any dinner for a week!" her voice raised to a fever pitch in staccato tones until Lana, shuddering, sat down and cried on her little chair.

She quickly moved to calm down her youngest child with soft, motherly tones. While what she did was necessary, Yustina sighed, not only over the drawing, but over her reaction.

options.name: Hate seeps even into the youngest ones

title: A Justified Military Reclamation
desc:
The village of Brilyakovo was awoken by the skid of truck tires and the shouting of voices as the 35th Motorized Infantry Division stormed the village. The steady footfalls of soldiers blended into those of panicked villagers, fleeing a potential German invasion.

A broad-shouldered officer contemptuously began to read out a prepared statement. “By command of the All-Russian Black League, this village is to be confiscated and turned over to the state in which it shall be used in our national defense. Any resistance to arrest will be met with gunfire at sight for treason."

Fearing the terror of the League, one by one, the villagers gave themselves up to the occupiers. Black-cloaked soldiers stomped to their houses, rounded the pedestrians up, and sent them to the village square. Any who resisted were beaten, or if they were unlucky, shot. Following this, they were corralled off to a few trucks, who'd send them away from everything they held dear. Only a scant 15 mix of rebellious youth and aging elders protested. However, instead of pushing and shoving, the officer simply began reading from a list of crimes they'd apparently committed against Russia.

Then, the officer raised his gloved hand, snapped his fingers, and the group was no more. In ten minutes, they were thrown into a snowy ditch. In just four hours, nothing and nobody remained. The good people of Russia would later learn that they were "attacked by Nazi Sympathizers" during the construction of state infrastructure. Despite the errant rumbling, nobody seemed to care, and certainly nobody did anything about it.

The construction was underway, and progress was steady. The village was going to become a military base for the preparations for the Great Trial. The forward military base would serve as a vanguard in the assault towards the plunderers in "Moskowien". This station, merely one of many, will be crucial in our fight against the Teutonic Menace.

options.name: An inevitable act for a noble cause.

title: This Is My Shovel
desc:
Life in the city of Dimitrovgrad was one of constant struggle for the people living there. Ever since 1941, it seemed that the residents of the average city could never truly catch a break. But recently, it seemed like they could, after Yazov had the previous owners of the city "decommissioned", life in Dimitrovgrad continued on without any real issues from the government, other than the odd military recruitment drives and so-on.

It was nice, but it couldn't last forever.

Early morning, on another seemingly average day, about five dozen soldiers poured into the city. They began going door to door and ordering the two most fit members of the family outside, once they had 52 people total. All of them odered into trucks, where they were told they were needed by the army and woulld fulfill their patriotic duty on this day.

Any questions asked were waved off and were replied with "When we arrive there, our commander will explain.". When they did arrive, all of them were ordered to dismount and line-up in age order. An officier in full League gard approached, and began to speak with a voice that exuded authority and confidence. "That way" he pointed "Is the Germans. High command has issued an express order that we should be prepared in-case any fights were to break out between us and them. So, you are going to dig two kilometers of trenches. By digging these trenches you are saving the lives of servicemen of the Russian Army. Get to work!"

And so they did Digging trenches was hard work that not all of them were used to, but with the amount of people there, it took them only about 3 hours to get the job completed to the officer's approval. Without so much as a word of praise they were then right after directed to leave the area immediately. They got back into the trucks and were driven back to the city. There were no words shared on the truck ride back, but it was obvious what everyone sitting there was thinking.

options.name: The dawn of the Great Trial was rapidly approaching.

title: Little Eyes, Little Ears
desc:
Arseniy tread with haste throughout the hallway of the bureau, folders in hand, a line to the United States straight behind the cold metal doors in front of him. He swung them open with great elan, slamming them into the utilitarian, off-white spackle. He set the folders down on the counter and booted up the computers. He jogged through the room, fiddling with knobs, setting the radios to the right frequency to call for help. The fax machine was already on, as he hoped. Everything was going swimmingly, and if it continued to do so, no one would ever know that Arseniy Nikolaev set foot in this building.

He’d had enough of it. Every day his son, Nikita, would come back from school, ranting about whatever new insanity the League invented that week, drilling him to become the perfect meat shield for the coming German onslaught. Every day his wife came back home more depressed, the tears of a woman separated from her family by the cadre system staining his white dress shirt. All of it, he’d had fucking enough. What the Americans knew was only a HINT of the true depravity of the League; soon enough, they’d get their impetus to act, god willing.

Arseniy was lost in thought until he realized something. The computers weren’t connecting to a network. The radios returned nothing but static. And the fax machine was on, but it wasn’t even working. His heart sank. The doors thumped as three men ran into the room, pistols in hand. At their front was Igor, the only officer of the League he ever managed to get along with, and the only friend he had ever made in the brutal rearrangement of the cadre system.

Igor thumbed the trigger on his pistol. “Arseniy. It is disappointing to find you here, truly.”

“H-How?”

“You raised a good kid.” Igor cocked the hammer of his gun and raised it up to Arseniy’s head.

options.name: “He’ll make a fine officer, one day.”

title: True League Comrades
desc:
In all of Ivan's life, he’d never once dared to betray the League. They were his protectors, and the ones who would strike down all who opposed his people’s enemies. And although he was only sixteen years of age, he believed himself to perhaps be the Leagues most faithful servant, taking every beating and scolding as a gift rather than a simple exercise of discipline.

Which is why he didn’t complain about being assigned to a League production facility. Upon arrival, he was in awe of the scale of these facilities, and just how intricately they were laid out. He had been assigned to a Cadre upon arrival, and was given instruction on how to operate the equipment on the production line by a fellow member of that Cadre. Within the hour, Ivan was working to produce the mechanisms of war that would assist in his nation's struggle.

He was perhaps the most zealous one there, being the first of a new type of Russian who had spent a majority of their time growing up knowing only the League and its constant flow of propaganda.

Ivan’s zealotry was exactly what the League needed, but he was a curse for the man sitting next to him, Valentin. He had never wanted to be here, and was forcefully assigned here years ago. He knew what happened to those who spoke out against the conditions, but had begun to reach his limit as the years went on. And when that day came, just a few hours after this new arrival had been assigned to work next to him, a man in an all black uniform came to inform them all of the new increase of production quotas, and the reduction in hours for break time.

He couldn’t restrain himself any longer, and let out a small whisper of defiance. “I hate this place and the godforsaken fools that lead it.”

Ivan heard every word. He swung his head over to look at the fool who dared speak against the League, but didn’t say a word. Later that day, he would report it to an official. And when he went to sleep, his bunkmate Valentin was there.

options.name: When he awoke, he was gone.

title: Great Russian Murals
desc:
Pavel wiped the sweat from his forehead, admiring the finished poster design. Like all his other works as of late, it had been commissioned. Well, 'commissioned' was a deeply charitable way of saying 'he had been told by a large, threatening man in a uniform to make it on pain of death whilst on minimal wages', but he was holding onto as much positivity as he could muster, given the circumstances.

He looked down upon what he had drawn, and felt alongside the token pride he took in his work, the familiar taste of bitterness. He was a cartoonist by trade. An illustrator. Before the Black League marched into his smaller city in West Russia, he had drawn cartoons of small animal people for children, living life and teaching them how to be kind to one another. His style had certainly developed over the years, that was for sure. Certainly not of his own volition, however.

Where he had once drawn soft, rounded shapes to appeal to the younger eye, he now drew sharp, angular lines. Lessons on life and getting along with one another were of no use to the Black League, nor was softness — only messages of triumph over the Teuton and the superiority of the Russian spirit would do. This was embodied in his piece — a chiseled man in a Black League uniform snapping the neck of Adolf Hitler.

The old artist sighed, looking at the time. 3:56AM. He still had 5 prompts to produce art for. Part of him wanted to doodle absent-midedly, but his paper usage was cataloged and he would be penalized financially for any 'wasted' paper. He checked the list once again. His next prompt, 'Russian Eagle disembowelling a German Eagle" would be fun to draw. Hopefully.

options.name: No room for creativity in the Great Trial.

title: A Safe Frontline
desc:
Pavel wiped the sweat from his brow, as his shovel dug into the dirt once more. He’d lost track of how long he’d been training, digging, building, and preparing for when his country would at last strike the Aryan, and drown him in his own blood. His brigade's training regimens had grown even more demanding than usual, but nobody complained. Every man knew what it was for, and some even welcomed the new torment brought upon them.

After all, every drop of blood, every broken bone, every moment of pain, was fuel. Fuel for the brave sons and daughters of the League who would exact vengeance on those who had defiled her, who had broken her and believed her incapable of returning to the world. Yet here they stood, ready to tear those scum limb from limb as the west burned in the fires of vengeance.

Pavel looked up from his part of the defensive works, and for the first time saw in their entirety the fruits of his and his comrades' work. Trenches and bunkers for miles, with a multitude of differently designed defensive works dug into the earth around them. Sadly his time for admiration quickly ended with the commanding officer's orders to get into formation. Pavel and his fellow soldiers assembled within seconds, forming an intricate pattern with each one standing at attention and ready for orders.

“Soldiers, I have received new orders pertaining to the extension of drilling procedures within the League. You shall now have only three separate five minute break periods per day, and you are required to complete a daily 12 mile run in place of the pre-existing 10 mile run. However, with the completion of all defensive works projects in this sector, you’re no longer to assist in their construction. Finally, the minimum accuracy in shooting range tests has been increased to 90%. Dismissed.”

Pavel and his 2 other friends found each other during the break period, and began to talk about things to come. Not about the new, unbelievably difficult demands laid upon their shoulders, but about a topic they had been betting upon for a while.

They each argued who would be the first to enter Moscow.

options.name: The warriors of a new age...

title: Burn Evidence, Burn Witnesses
desc:
Rule 15. Should a suspected person be found disseminating misinformation that undermines progress of the Great Trial, they are to be taken from their living area and put into interrogation until they reveal exactly which Teuton agency they are working for and who they have lied to. Upon revealing this, said person is to be executed.

Rule 16. Should a member of the police or any other security agency come into contact with any misinformative or deceptive Teuton propaganda, it is to be taken to the nearest town pyre and thrown in with any other Germanic materials. Only the cleansing fires can bring any merit out of their sordid materials.

Rule 17. Should a civilian act out against any member of the Black League or other official personnel, they are to be subdued by any means necessary. Punishment for doing so can range from two decades of service in a labor camp, rescindment of nuclear protections, a reduction of rations to any known familial relations, or point blank execution.

title: The Weaponization of Social Progress
desc:
It was odd, having Yuri out of the house so often. Nadya wandered through their shared apartment, as she often did nowadays, wafting aimlessly from room to room. The couple had only met recently, a few years ago at a book club in Tomsk. Yuri had always been a well-read man.

Part of her wanted to be distraught that her partner had been forced into working 14-hour shifts at the local munitions factory, seven days a week, and she was undoubtedly angry at not seeing him as much. But whilst he was gone, she had found herself digging into the secret stash of books that Yuri kept, hidden away where the Black League couldn't burn it for not being patriotic enough.

He was always too scared to share his collection with her, before. But because he was now too busy to even come close to stopping her, Nadya could do it, and when she did, she felt free. And she enjoyed that feeling more than anything.

Of course, she knew that Yazov had not done this out of some great feminist desire to liberate women, or something. Russia was not the place for that. But he had done something, inadvertently. As she curled up with Yuri's copy of War and Peace, Nadya mused about what else to do later on. It wasn't as if she'd be pressed for time, after all.

title: An Ear In Every Room
desc:
Nikolai Volkov was not a man to take things lightly. Suspicion was as much a part of his personality as his affinity for black tea or his love for classic Russian novels. Living in an aging apartment complex, he had a habit of paying a little too much attention to his surroundings.

This particular night was no exception. As the small town settled into its nocturnal routine, an unusual hush fell over his apartment. However, what caught his attention was the soft murmur of his neighbors' conversation seeping through the paper-thin wall separating their lives.

His heart pounded slightly harder in his chest, the tranquility of his demeanor replaced with an edge of anxiety. The conversation felt different, the cadence, the intensity. Even the silence between their words seemed to carry a certain gravity. Something was not right.

The words were veiled by the sturdiness of the wall, the specific sentences hard to decipher. Yet, certain phrases seemed to penetrate this barrier, filling his apartment, and his mind, with an unease. "It's coming sooner than we thought," he heard a man say. "We need to prepare. It could change everything," a woman responded.

A shiver ran down Nikolai's spine, his eyes narrowing with intrigue and suspicion. Was it a coded message? Could his seemingly ordinary neighbors be involved in some clandestine operation? As the minutes rolled into hours, he found himself increasingly drawn to this puzzle and soon enough found the answer in his troubled mind.

He rushed to pick up his old telephone and dial 'Line One.' A heavily distorted voice echoed through the receiver, “You have reached the Complaints Secretariat, do you have a concern to report?”

Drawing in a deep breath, Nikolai found the words he needed, the declaration that felt both chilling and necessary, "I do. I think my neighbors are spies.”

options.name: “It’s a boy, Anatoly... it’s a boy...”

title: Produce Only What You Need
desc:
A loud knock was on the door followed by an order to open the door immediately. A worker rushed to the door and opened it. It was a Black League officer. The officer demanded to speak to the owner. He said that this factory had been creating too many luxury products and should instead focus on producing only what the community and army needs. The workers called the owner out. The owner was annoyed, but came quickly.

“What is i-”

His heart stopped whenever he saw the officer.

“Your factory has been deemed to not be complying with the government's regulations. You have been creating too many luxury goods.”

The owner started biting his nails, he knew that it was illegal to produce luxury goods, however it was very lucrative and had generated an immense amount of wealth for him.

“Are you insane? You fools are destroying Russia! How are we supposed to earn a living here if business can’t flourish without the government sticking their nose where they shouldn’t!”

“I will not repeat myself, cease production or else you will be terminated.”

The owner thought for a moment. Would he really be willing to sacrifice all of this wealth just for some doomed war? Why did they have to come into power? Russia would’ve been prosperous under any other government but we had to get stuck with these fools.

“Mere bluffing will not stop me. I am one of the biggest industrialists in all of Russia, do you really think you can terminate me without any consequences?”

The officer sighed, and calmly reached for his pistol.

title: Acceptance is Defeat
desc:
Rows of workers, hoping to find some respite from the grueling labor that was their lives from dawn to dusk, were instead sitting before a projector, soldiers in black uniforms guarding the exits. A few of the workers squirmed in their chairs, the uncomfortable seating compounding the aching in their muscles. At the front of them all stood an officer, gesturing to the wall on which the projection was playing.

"Here you see the bodies of the dead. The German beasts have mutilated their corpses for the crime of rebellion. These are your fellow Russians, those who seek to be redeemed in the struggle against our eternal foe. This is what they are doing at this very moment, and what they hope to do to all of us should they succeed in their plans."

The film showed a mass grave that had been dug by some of the other slaves working in the Reichskommissariat Moskowien. Men, women, and children were lying in a mountain of bodies, with bullet holes and gashes where bayonets had pierced their skin. The film then shifted as a group of soldiers harassed a woman who had attempted to kill one of the officers. They tore at her clothing, enough for the men to begin raping her. Some of the workers looked away on instinct, not wanting to continue watching. Only the mere movement of the men in black out of the corner of their eyes snapped their attention back towards the projection.

After the men had finished with her, one of them took out a knife and began stabbing her. A game of sorts had started as the soldiers began cutting at her as if to carve mementos from her body. She was only screaming for a few short moments before she lay dead. By the end, she was missing both her ears, a hand, and a breast, and her stomach had been cut open. The film ended here.

"See the hatred that the Germans feel for us, and know that we will show them retribution. They will feel our wrath–our vengeance–and justice will be served to every last one of them."[Change Later]

options.name: Shock and horror give way to rage.

title: Goodbyes at Fifteen
desc:
The bugle’s call clawed at the morning fog, yanking Ivan from his thin mattress. Cold and barefoot, the fifteen-year-old recruit snapped to attention like he had done every day for the past five months. Thirty-two other recruits of similar age fell into formation next to their beds, an unbroken line of adolescent determination stretching down the length of the barracks.

Exactly twenty-three seconds after the horn sounded, their drill officer stormed into the room. His eyes held a glint that spoke of a perpetual bad mood and a determination to instil order and discipline in his charges.

"Kozlov! Fix that blasted posture now!" His words sliced through the morning chill. "Are you planning on marching into Germany looking like a hunchback?"

Kozlov stumbled over his response, the young cadet wilting under scrutiny. "Y-yes sir! It won’t happen again."

"Damn right it won't," growled the officer. His gaze swept over them all, eyes as piercing and cold as the winds outside. "We are the chosen, the ones to reclaim our homeland's glory. We are the instruments of the Great Trial, and we will not fail!" His gaze found Ivan's, a silent understanding passing between them. "Ivanov," he said, a new edge of severity cutting through his voice, "You were the first to arrive at the training field yesterday, were you not?"

"Yes sir, I was." Ivan's voice held steady under the scrutiny.

The officer grunted, a sound trapped between approval and scorn. "Good. Make sure you're the first one today as well, or it's extra drills for you."

As the officer moved on, Ivan set his gaze straight ahead, a grim smile tugging at his lips. His day had just begun. The whispered dreams of home from the night before lingered, but there was no time for dreams here, only duty.

options.name: The Motherland has no need for sentimentalism.

title: Второй шаг
desc:
Человек летел вдалеке от Земли.

Миллионы наблюдали за этим героическим полетом, и то, что многие считали первым разом, когда человек осмелился ступить на чужую землю, транслировалось по всему миру.

Великие нации застыли в тишине, когда Шаттл шатко вышел из атмосферы колыбели человечества, сломил броню, которая защищала их, и начал свой путь к Луне, которая была свидетелем всего безумия человечества и всех человеческих побед.

Безмолвные звучали громче говорящих, пока шаттл медленно приземлялся на серого наблюдателя. Люди медленно выходили из своего металлического сосуда и наблюдали за пейзажем, недоступного человеку, кроме как в телескоп. Они гордо прыгнули вперед с флагом в руке, транслируя свои слова на всеобщее обозрение.

Но то, что они увидели вдалеке, удивило их.

Миссия изменилась, смятение нарастало. Исследователи отважились уйти далеко-далеко от того места, где они изначально планировали остаться. И там они нашли еще один флаг, давно побелевший на поверхности бесчисленными веками. В тот момент миллионы ученых, историков и археологов сидели с разинутыми ртами, а то, что когда-то было сказкой, унаследованной с незапамятных времен, смотрело на них, как будто бросая вызов этим новым нарушителям правды.

Они осторожно сняли флаг и заменили его их собственным. Последний нетронутый памятник погибшему человечеству, доставленный домой для изучения и наблюдения. Возможно, до тех пор, пока на поверхности Луны не будет водружен следующий флаг.

options.name: И как мечтали их предки, так и мечтали они...

title: RAD.14.t
desc:
Первый год после конца был самым тяжелым. Массовый голод, болезни, радиация - смерть надежды. Когда человечество мерцало и угасало, большинство полагало, что их смерть будет забыта, как и весь род человеческий. Каждое достижение, каждое красивое произведение искусства, каждый вопящий ребенок, принесенный из утробы матери в усталые руки матери - это все было бессмысленной тратой? Космологическая странность вскоре исчезла из-за разрушительного воздействия времени.

Все началось по-разному, в разных местах, и в некоторых заняло больше времени, чем в других. Но первые воспоминания о старом мире начались через год после того, как упали бомбы - плюс-минус несколько восходов солнца. В Германии разбитые остатки батальонов будут проводить имитацию артиллерийского салюта своим павшим братьям, сохраняя только пулю, чтобы встретить ужас конца. В Америке священники и их паства находили все безопасные места, чтобы установить сотни крестов в честь павших патриотов. В Японии святыни строили из металлолома, щебня и любого другого мусора, который можно было собрать, чтобы успокоить беспокойных духов.

Сначала это было спонтанно, и люди прилагали к этому усилия только в том случае, если могли себе это позволить, отнимая время от выживания. Но шли годы, и каждая культура делала все возможное, чтобы сохранить живую память по-своему старому миру. В Британии выжившие выкладывали маки и венки, и любые другие цветы в память о призраках Альбиона. В России мужчины встречались в этот день, чтобы выпить за память погибших сыновей Родины. От Северной и Южной Америки до Океании, от глубин Африки до дальних уголков Азии, умершие почитаемы.

Даже когда последние напоминания о старом мире стали мифами, а память о том, что именно случилось, была забыта, народы продолжали оплакивать то, что было потеряно. Эмпайр Стейт посвятил парады и стихи предкам, потерянным в древнем пламени. Племя Мухлар проводило большую охоту каждый год в день, который они считали днем конца. На Сионе, под куполом Третьего Храма проводились молитвы, чтобы благословить древних мертвецов и поблагодарить за их собственное выживание.

Однажды человек ступит на Луну и найдет древний выбеленный флаг. Он будет смотреть на Землю и вспоминать тех, кто ступил сюда задолго до этого и читать тихое стихотворение в их память.

options.name: При закате солнца и утром нового дня - Мы их запомним.

title: RAD.8.t
desc:
В результате взрыва тысяч ядерных зарядов поверхность Земли превратилась в тонкий слой пепла, а атмосфера была загрязнена радиоактивными частицами, которые сделали воздух токсичным. Однако, за пределами мира, который создал и затем уничтожил человек, артефакты человечества все еще сохранились в целости и сохранности. По крайней мере, один из них все еще функционировал.

R4O был четвертым и последним из серии научных спутников Земли программы "Разведка и наблюдение", запущенных Соединенными Штатами для военных и научных целей в 1960-х годах. В военном плане оказались совершенно бесполезными в чем-либо, кроме предупреждения Белого дома о неминуемом уничтожении после того, как ракеты начали свою судную миссию, но именно их научные возможности возможно окажутся более полезными для человечества еще долго после того, как военная функция их выполнила свою роль.

Три из четырех, вместе с большинством искусственных спутников вокруг Земли, перестали функционировать после того, как случился апокалипсис, и в конечном итоге рухнули на поверхность. Однако курс R4O был грамотно рассчитан, и, что наиболее важно, станция управления на Земле, которая передавала ей инструкции, была автоматизирована и избежала взрывов, оставшись невредимой. Когда в тот роковой день погибли миллиарды людей, R4O продолжал наблюдать за ними. Он видел, как тысячи огней, которые когда-то освещали синий шарик ночью, внезапно погасли, миллионы людей, которые с надеждой смотрели на спутники в бескрайние дали, внезапно ушли под землю или покинули это бренный мир. Спустя время, свидетель ада на Земле увидел кое-что интересное, среди абсолютной темноты или отражения лучей солнца от Земли. Что-то вдохновляющее. Что-то, что вселяет надежду на то, что человечество все еще готово к великим открытиям.

Он видел, как горят несколько огней в отдаленных местах планеты.

title: RAD.5.t
desc:
Michael was in the car's driver seat. Sweat dripped down his face, and he looked at his clock nervously. For 8 minutes, the traffic had not moved one inch on the highway. 8 minutes and 1 second. 2 seconds. 3 seconds. He looked outside. As always, cars could be seen for kilometers ahead. Near him, a fistfight had broken out between two strangers. One of them pulled out a gun, ending the argument quickly. Then, he saw some people taking the insane decision to abandon their cars, and make a run for it on foot. Insane, right? Or was it?

He quickly opened the seat's door. He took the backpack of supplies he had brought with him, and started running. He ran along the road, occasionally stepping on vehicles, and did not stop for any reason. Those who watched Michael lost track of him when he slipped through the dense trees, heading for the forest.

Running was getting exhausting. With every step he took, he felt like a giant carrying his entire weight. He continued running, not stopping until the dark covered the sky, and the night set in. However, surviving these 8 hours of darkness in the woods was not as simple as Michael thought. Animals were easy to fight with a Swiss army knife and a torch; other humans, not so much. Exhausted and injured, he eventually sat down under a tree. He stayed there, until the sun finally rose over the horizon. Except it was not the sun, but a device of destruction. The view of the explosion would surely be majestic, but would only last for a second before causing complete blindness. Instead, Michael waited patiently for the shockwave to come, just like last time, and it came, throwing him down. Once that was done, he knew there was only one option. Run away from civilization, the one that destroyed itself, and nature with it.

options.name: Назад к природе, к нашим корням.

title: RAD_EU.111.t
desc:
Deep within the earth, men stood at attention as their commanding officer came in. All wore the same garb. All wore the same helmets and hats, with twin lightning bolts on the sides. All had received the final briefing for their mission. The silos would no longer be silent. Men filed to consoles, controls, and prepared their final targets. Coordinates were punched in, rockets were prepared, and as the commanding officer marched past the two portraits of the Fuhrer and Reichsfurher to his position, one of the men at the controls had... doubt.

Billions of men and women and children would die by his hand at the press of a few buttons. The world itself would collapse. Everything of the past, everything of the world would be burnt away and there would be nothing left. He turned for a moment and eyed the portraits of the Reich's leader and Burgundy's own, both wearing the same caps with the same lightning bolts as his own. They were responsible. He wasn't to blame. He was just following orders.

Just following orders. He pressed a few buttons as the rockets armed, only to pause again. Just following orders. Could he really justify that much blood? All those deaths, simply because he was told it was for a greater good he couldn't see. No. He was hiding his guilt with cowardice. Cowardice which-

"Why have you not continued the launch sequence?" A harsh tone of voice grated into his mind, carving through his train of thought. The commander was looking at him. They were all looking at him.

He couldn't do it. He couldn't let them do it. A single, final cry of refusal exited his mouth as he reached for his pistol.

options.name: A launch was delayed by three minutes.

title: RAD_EU.107.t
desc:
Somewhere in the corpse of a mighty Reich, a band of scavengers discovered a single storehouse of glass bottles and containers with weird symbols on them none in the group could understand. Selling the boxes to collectors as 'relics', and passing them around to any who desired crates, the scavengers were initially glad to have made a profit through the trade of these small amenities.

Days later, when several of the scavengers began vomiting uncontrollably and convulsing, there were many who regretted ever stepping into the storehouse and others who quickly understood the gravity of the situation. A debate arose on whether or not to turn back, and the group split, with some demonizing the cowardice of others, while others demonized the folly of their brethren.

Many did not make it back to the places they had traded with, but several finally returned and discovered to their horror that the worst had indeed come. Vomit filled the streets, men and women covered in boils and sores along with it. Plenty would turn away from the land, citing it and those who lived there as cursed, but others would stay. Doctors tried strange and peculiar treatments, others searched for clues on the contents of the boxes through ancient archives, and even those who could not help did their best to bring doctors what was asked, or warn strangers of the land's current ailment.

For now, however, a long dead hand strangles thousands in its grip.

options.name: They will find a cure. Eventually.

title: RAD_EU.89.t
desc:
The squad of SS soldiers had grown fat and happy in their bunker, protected from the annihilation caused by the Great War. They were supposed to be a crack team of well prepared ruthless Aryan fighters, ready to come out in the aftermath of the war and quickly clean up any would-be resistance to their resettlement plans. Instead of training however, the group were so confident in their abilities that they spent most of their time in the bunker partying and drinking. They even ignored what time they were supposed to arise from the bunker to reclaim the land, to instead spend more drunken nights in the cozy shelter.

When they finally arose from the bunker after exhausting much of their supplies, they lazily grabbed their weapons and equipment and psyched themselves to stomp any savage who would dare stand in their way. It would be easy pickings most of them thought, how could it not be? They were the chosen ones after all.

After opening the bunker door, it only took a couple of steps out in the open for the squad commander to stumble over a tripwire and be blown to smithereens. The rest of the squad, shell-shocked and stunned, were like fish in a barrel for the assortment of hidden away young men and women who gunned down the SS troopers with reckless abandon. Decked out in plain black garbs and tucked away in trees and bushes, the would be future of the Aryan race was nothing short of obliterated by the young guerrillas.

As one survivor gazed up at the group who had surrounded his near dead body, their faces lacking any empathy for the soon to be deceased man, he could only think to ponder the fate of his homeland now that these degenerates had seemingly come to rule it. Before he could even begin to preach these malicious dying thoughts to the group of youngsters, he was promptly shot straight in the head and left for the vultures along with the rest of his SS squad.

options.name: It's our world now, mein kameraden.

title: RAD_EU.81.t
desc:
Many years after the apocalypse, in a place that was once one of the cruelest, horrendous Reichskommissariats in Europe, bunkers opened and families slowly, tentatively came out. They did not all speak the same language, nor did they share the same ideas and goals. However, though many could and would likely fight each other violently in the future, there was no strife within the first few weeks.

In fact, among many of the older members of the bunkers, there was a similar reaction of camaraderie and awe; for the first thing to surprise them was the colors. A bright blue sky without even a hint of the smothering, sinking gray fog that had drowned out the horizon for years. Plants, green and growing. Where there had been a once baleful red eye hanging above, glaring through the smog at those toiling and suffering below, a gold disk hung, bright and shining.

The elderly laughed and sobbed, and the children questioned for weeks and months to follow, and even though several couldn't speak the same language, they understood pointing. The older ones would point at what appeared to be a miracle to them and laugh among themselves, while for a time the younger ones questioned each other, getting different words for different things. Groups of people who would have never tolerated each other before began to mingle, all brought together by a single miraculous change of colors.

options.name: Perhaps there is hope for peace after all.

title: RAD_EU.73.t
desc:
Erik knew that this day would come. Between war and peace, mankind always seemed to prefer the former. His friends and family mocked him when he said he would be living at the Vault for the foreseeable future. Now they were dead. He was a man with no family and two friends: the Vault, and one of the assholes who helped him run it.

He sighed, pushing the papers on his desk aside while somberly sipping a cup of coffee. This was the end, and his work had just begun. Standing from his desk, he walked down the cavernous, chilly hallway towards the seed vault. He knew every inch of the massive warehouse, where each and every plant species known to humanity was stored. There were so many he could name from memory alone: over a thousand plant species had been catalogued from nearly every nation. Authoritarian or free, capitalist, communist, fascist, whatever; most nations sent seeds as a last contingency.

Erik wondered what seed he should choose as the first to be planted again. He had no access to tropical areas as of yet, so any plants native to that area were out of the question. Scandinavian cold narrowed the shortlist further, and the need to thrive in more temperate areas winnowed the field to a few choice candidates. Wheat, the first crop ever grown by man, would be poetically fitting, but there was no true way to know the best choice.

Walking into cold storage, the superchilled air caressed Erik's face, and he realized that it did not matter which plant he chose; it would be years before any were planted. Perhaps that was to be his lot in life, to be the agrarian vanguard of the new age. He sighed deeply, unsure, unready, unknowing of what the future would hold for Erik the Reclaimer.

title: RAD_EU.71.t
desc:
Wilhelm Lange floated comfortably in the crew compartment of Reich, a temporary space station set to last no more than 3 months. He checked his watch; 7 AM in Germania, night shift at mission control would be switching over to the day crew. He buzzed over the comm, "Germania Control, this is Reich, we are currently over the Mediterranean, internal temperature is nominal, all systems green."

No response was given. Wilhelm was just about to request a copy when one of the Reich's 3 crew, Johann Weber, called out to him. "Commandant, come to the cupola. You need to see this."

Wilhelm sighed and lazily flung himself down the main living area of Reich, towards the viewing cupola on the opposite end of the station. Reaching the large, semi-spherical cupola window, Weber pointed at Rome on the Earth below. "Yes, that's Rome," he said dismissively, "What of it?"

"It's glowing orange. In the day."

"Oh... oh god."

Lange and Weber sat in silence as a glowing blaze of reddish flame swallowed the city of Rome, hundreds of kilometers below them. In the distance, over the small area of Earth they could see with the naked eye, bright, fleeting flashes of light danced over the major cities of Europe. Germania Control did not respond because Germania no longer existed.

For several hours, the crew of Reich could do little but sit in solemn silence, and watch their race burn from a vantage point in the heavens.

title: RAD_EU.68.t
desc:
If she was going to do it, it had to be now. How long had she waited for this day? Ten years at least, although it felt like an entire lifetime for Sarah Frank, a second generation slave who had spent all of her life toiling in the work camps of Ostland. Not one day longer though, for today she was a free woman, able to spend her last day in whatever manner she chose, and she knew damn well what she was about to spend it on. There was a particular SS officer who was about to die, painfully at that.

She paused to consider the thought that this final act of vengeance would soon be rendered utterly meaningless. Weren't they all going to die in the imminent nuclear war? Wasn't the only reason she and the other slaves were able to escape that the guards had all panicked and abandoned their posts? Would not her final hours be better spent with her remaining family? No, she decided quickly and finally, this had to happen. Just because the bastard was almost certainly going to die in the flames of Armageddon didn't mean her mission was meaningless. It mattered how that man would die, it mattered that she would be the one to end his life, it mattered that even if it could only happen in the final moments of history, someone stood up to that man and exacted well-earned justice.

She knew where he would go. Had he not subjected Sarah and her fellow slaves to forced stints in brothels for his sick amusement often enough? He would be there, she was certain. As it turned out, she was able to reach the disreputable den before he did, allowing her to find the perfect hiding spot to ambush her prey. She didn't need to wait long. As he stumbled toward the door in a drunken stupor, she had him in her grasp. She didn't take pleasure in what she had done to the officer, but neither did she feel any remorse or guilt. She had delivered just retribution, and her only regret was that nukes were about to do her job for her for the rest of them.

title: RAD_EU.67.t
desc:
How many ways can one say goodbye? How many different combinations of words can be created to express a farewell to life, love, and humanity? Communications Officer Gunther Hermann was finding out the answer. Too damn many ways, as it turned out. So many ways, he didn't want to continue hearing any of them any more. But he had to, he thought as the tears began to roll unbidden down his cheeks, those poor bastards deserved to have someone, anyone at all, hearing their last words.

It wasn't supposed to have been like this, of course. He had never expected a war with the United States to actually come. Everything had gone well up until now, wasn't all of Europe back firmly under German dominance for the first time since the War? But no, for the Führer to have actually gone ahead with the invasion of America... It was too late for unanswerable questions and half-baked theories. Whatever the reason, it had happened. He didn't have much longer to listen. As he put back on the headset connecting his station to a field headquarters somewhere, Florida perhaps? He wasn't thinking quite clearly enough to determine, he heard the sound of a male voice. It was deep, military rough, and the kind of voice that was supposed to sound strong and reassuring. The voice was sobbing. "My god! My god! It's all over... everything. I don't want to die. Please God, just let me see my children and I pro-" A gunshot. The voice stopped.

He didn't want to listen to the rest. As he put the headset down, he could hear muffled screaming from the other end. It went to static as he slowly walked out of the command center, directly into a bright, embracing light.

options.name: Do not go gently into that good night.

title: RAD_EU.66.t
desc:
Of course none of the musicians had left the hall. Why would they bother? Where would they go? Nothing could be done to avert their fates, they were going to die. Perhaps if one observed the behaviors of one million groups at the end of the world, only one of those million would have no members panic or leave, but as impossible as it seemed, none left the hall. They were going to die very soon. That was why they were playing Mozart's Requiem. It seemed funny, in a very disturbing sort of way, to the wizened old Conductor, to play such a song. As he picked up his baton, he let out a derisive chuckle, "I'm not sure about you all, but I never imagined I'd go out listening to Mozart myself. I happen to be more of a Schubert man to be honest." A few laughs, a handful of grunts, maybe a sob. It didn't matter one bit to the Conductor if they found his gallows humor funny or not. He had already begun to stir up the strings.

The music picked up in earnest, all at once like water rushing out from a bursting dam. The Conductor had always preferred to have his orchestra play in smaller venues or better yet, privately, for the music's sake. Yet as heard the strains of the violins, the wave-like rolling of the cellos, what he wished for more than anything was an audience. How they would have marveled, how they would have been enraptured! The frantic, desperate air of inevitable destruction that was given to the playing was elevating this performance high above any that had ever been heard by mortal ears, the Conductor thought to himself as he let his baton drop. They no longer needed direction; they were being carried along by devotion to the craft, devotion to beauty.

The music seemed to finish as quickly and as suddenly as it had begun, the echoes of the last refrain hanging heavily in the air. The Conductor had just time enough to wipe the tears forming in his eyes and say to his performers, "Thank you all. That was truly marvelous."

title: RAD_EU.61.t
desc:
The scene in the room was nothing short of bacchanalian. Dropped food, spilled wine, and shards from broken bottles littered the ground. People in various states of undress were eating and drinking with reckless abandon, while others were scampering off to whatever empty bed or deserted corner they could find for one last roll in the hay.

Others may have wanted to head home and spend a moment with their loved ones, or praying in a church, or do anything but spend their final day in a hazy, drug-and-sex-filled stupor. But these brave sons and daughters of the Vaterland didn't have those options, all removed from their hometowns and shuffled around the Reich for whichever military or bureaucratic jobs needed staffing. Happenstance had brought them together, and they were going to die together, so why not have some fun? They were about to be denied all of life's pleasures forever, so they made up for lost time by trying them all at once.

As the minutes slipped by and more radio stations grew silent, the pace of the party got more frenzied. The final drops of alcohol were eagerly drunk, bellies were stuffed with every morsel of food, and tablets of Pervitin were passed around and swallowed like candy. The newscaster said it was ninety minutes to impact, right? Whenever it was, they all wanted to go out numb when it happened.

The ninetieth minute passed with nothing of note. Then the ninety-first. At the end of the ninety-second, one of the revelers asked "Do you think they-"

And then it happened.

title: RAD_EU.58.t
desc:
Captain McDougall steadily guided his tanker towards Port Glasgow. Times had been tumultuous recently, but he rested easily at night, knowing this haul was going to net him a tidy bonus. After all, his boat carried 320,000 deadweight tons of crude black gold, direct from the heart of Texas. It had been a long voyage across the Atlantic, but the trip was going to be well worth it.

Then it happened. First, a bright, burning light illuminated the ship as if a million spotlights had been trained on it. McDougall had no time to comprehend this before a blast from afar rocked the ship and tore apart the hull. McDougall barely understood what was happening, but he knew what he had to do. He ordered all men off the ship. He organized a swift gathering to the lifeboats. One by one, his crew embarked. After the last men had gotten away safely, McDougall cut the boat's line's loose and remained aboard. The last his crew saw of him, he was lighting up one last cigarette and flicking the match into the leaking oil.

The crew would soon make it to a southerly island between two greater lands. Though there were never any shortages of hardships in their community, they always would remember or be reminded of the old Captain when tensions rose. He served as a model for all to follow, someone who was willing to give up all his goals and even his life if it meant saving others.

title: RAD_EU.54.t
desc:
A Field Held in Time:: "What do you see friend?" John said to Malcolm, staring across the vastness of the land. "Nothing... only shadows." Malcolm replied uneasily.

The two men had been held in the field for days now. Or wait...was it weeks? Years perhaps? Who knows anymore. Who cares.

What the two men were tasked to find, under the watchful eye of their ever-present supervisor, was a great treasure in this field. Their boss was certain of it, he only required a "keener eye". It was apparently why he conjured up Malcolm and John, in order to get them to help him find it. The field proved mystical in its workings though. The men looked long and hard for the treasure said to be buried here, but found very little in terms of material items. Instead, they had only each other, united in the fear of the boss' retribution should they fail in their task.

"God is punishing us." John stated to Malcolm as they dug through the ground using only their hands.

"What for?" Malcolm asked.
 "Everything" said John wearily.

Days, hours, months or weeks past. Who could really tell. What the two men could tell, however, was when they eventually found the treasure.

"Boss, boss! It's here, we found it!" shouted Malcolm, with tears in his eyes.
 "Well done, my lads," acknowledged the boss "now let us see it."

The boys stepped back from the pit to show off their findings, and what the boss saw pleased him deeply. Down in the ground lay a massive unexploded bomb, just waiting to be taken. One could only imagine its possibilities.

options.name: It is truly remarkable what one finds in his own back garden.

title: RAD_EU.53.t
desc:
Your father will be looking for you, Fraulein Strauss."

Some shuffling, taut muscle brushing against soft, supple skin, before the cold reply. "I've made my choice."

Fraulein Strauss always had her way -- or else. Her stubbornness was tiring most times, some times endearing. This time, it frustrated him. The air sirens kept blaring their infernal noise outside. The grandfather clock ticked and tocked, edging closer to the end of the world. "There's still time before they reach Germania," Yosef pleaded. "You need to get dressed and leave. The rest of the estate won't go until you-"

The kiss caught him off guard. Memories of warmth and bliss rushed to the forefront; for a brief moment, he returned it with the passion he had shown her not an hour ago.

"Dumpkopf. Hold me closer," Fraulein Strauss said after pulling back, smiling and eyes glazed. He hesitated.

"That is an order." A brief, uneasy moment of silence, then a weight settling itself back on his chest. "Please. Yosef," came the murmur.

The servant obliged, wrapping an arm around her small figure. His chin rested on her smooth, white locks. "Wilma, I promised to keep you safe. I'll be fine."

"And you promised not to leave my side, no?" Yosef had no answer, to his shame. Suddenly, he felt her figure tremble, hot liquid spill onto bare skin. "Just... just let me have this," Wilma begged shakily. She continued, "Please. Please..." A stream became a torrent, flowing freely, as her words faded into whispers.

Sighing, Yosef rubbed small circles on Wilma's back. Fraulein Strauss demanded his obedience. His... lover... asked something of him. Who was he to refuse either way?

With a peck on her forehead, Yosef wrapped his arms around Wilma and pulled her close. He felt her own settle gently on his back.

options.name: In the end, they never left the other.

title: RAD_EU.48.t
desc:
Auguste had never been to Paris. He had never seen the golden glow of a city of life and light and grandeur. As far as he was concerned, however, this was not Paris. No life filled the bustling streets with people. No light gleamed through broad avenues and narrow alleyways. No grandiose monuments to a now dead nation stood tall.

This was a city of shadows. A city of silence and shadows and toiling spirits. Amidst the rubble of the shattered streets, imprints in the shape of men and women and children were printed on the bricks and concrete of walls and stairs and roads. Everywhere Auguste went, the shadows followed, scattered throughout the ruins. They remained an echo of the day that Paris was razed to ashes. The memory of those who made the shadows would soon fade, washed away like a footprint on a beach.
