Life in the bunker was a continuous, unchanging cycle: work, off-duty, go home to sleep, then wake up for the next day's work, off-duty······ Only in the last half month had the material allocations clearly decreased. Yurika knew that the next round of surface exploration was about to begin; after all, this was not the first time. Several of his friends had already vanished in the ruins and the wasteland, but he had been relatively lucky, surviving until now.

Sure enough, not long after work began in the morning, a young man wearing a black hat came into the factory and ascended the platform usually off-limits for speeches: "For the League, for the Great Trial, by any means necessary, we must raise enough food! Fighters of the League, your deeds shall live forever!"

Before the Commissar's slogans had faded, Yurika and some colleagues were sent to a similarly ruined city with some dilapidated gear. He knew these slogans were only for the newcomers. The outside was no sanctuary; bandits, contamination, chemical weapons leaks, leftover landmines, and other weapons······ anything could take their lives. He could only sigh and teach his rookie partner some survival knowledge and material identification methods: "If a place looks very clean, run immediately. It means there are definitely people nearby, and you can't be sure if they belong to the League. If there are obvious signs of human presence, run even faster. Packaged medicines and food outside are usually fine; take them. Some things that look very industrially manufactured can be extremely valuable, but they are also very rare. Also······"

······

To his surprise, they didn't even see a soul during this operation, and the assembly time had already arrived. They were walking down the street with a large box full of canned goods and a radio that still worked. "God bless······ Anastasia··· and my unborn child······" Just when he thought he had escaped danger this time as before, a sudden anomaly occurred.

With a sharp 'Click!', an uncleared pressure-activated landmine exploded under his foot.

Before he could have another thought, Yurika was reduced to a pile of fragmented flesh.

The young man reported the accident, and the number '18140' was crossed out from the ledger of the Quartermaster Department and the Ground Reconnaissance Dispatch Team.

options.name: The poor man's wife didn't even know how her husband died.

title: The Widow
desc:
Anastasia suffered from insomnia all night. Only when the loudspeaker reminded people it was time to wake up did she struggle to climb out of bed, but her soul was already preoccupied with her husband Yurika and had not returned.

Since Yurika left yesterday morning to search for supplies, she hadn't received a single piece of news all day. Normally, Yurika would be home by five or six in the evening at the latest, when the hands of the clock hanging on the factory wall reached that point, and he would tell her about the dangers and interesting things he encountered outside. She knew in her heart that this abnormality definitely did not mean good news—perhaps a serious injury that would affect the operation, or······ she could only pray that the worst possibility hadn't happened.

With an anxious heart, she tidied herself up, preparing to continue her day, because she knew that asking people in the League was useless. The bureaucrats would only fob her off with meaningless nonsense. However, just then, there was a knock on the door.

"Hello? Who is it?"

"Madam, this is your exclusive certificate. You may present it at the distribution station to exchange for one and a half times the regular ration quota. It is for you and your child. I am the Captain of the League's 33687 Ground Reconnaissance Dispatch Team, and I am here to inform you: your husband, 18140, was unfortunately killed during a reconnaissance mission the day before yesterday. Cause of death: shot by bandits."

Anastasia stood stunned for two seconds, and then the color drained from her face: "I··· I understand."

The Captain saluted her, then turned and left as if nothing had happened.

options.name: Everything was as normal, save for the solitary card.

title: Modernizing Military Training
desc:
Military training used to be a rather easy task for Sokolov. It didn't matter to him how strict the standards were or how many died during the training; what did a few deaths of unfit men matter in the vastness of Russia? There would always be patriotic men to fill the ranks.

However, this simple job is now starting to give Sokolov a headache. The environment underground is far inferior to the surface. Even with the League constructing massive ventilation systems, the amount of air a person can breathe each day is limited. He had a platoon of soldiers exercise for a morning according to the old standards, but the Security Department informed him to stop the training—their breathing capacity was already nearing the daily waste-air processing limit.

Then there are the training standards. The old army would default to sending soldiers to the harshest environments, giving them minimal gear, forcing them to return to the camp on their own, and then subjecting them to 'pain education' during their reception, to teach them discipline and forge the strongest-willed and most capable soldiers. But last week, a fool in the forces did just that. He ended up killing more than a dozen men, and the rest lost their combat effectiveness due to starvation. The superiors immediately sent him to a penal battalion.

The old standards won't work, but the job still needs to be done. Sokolov paced back and forth in his office for a long time before finally devising a solution. He cut the original long-distance cross-country into short-duration bursts, eliminated all explosive exercises, and increased the training volume for basic movements like standing at attention and crawling. For the remaining time, thankfully, there were plenty of books and video materials in the training hall; he'd just have them catch up on their reading and viewing.

He nervously submitted this heavily revised training regimen. A short while later, the directive from above arrived: Approved.

title: Wasteland Survival Education
desc:
"Hello everyone, and welcome to 'The Principles of Rebirth,' sponsored by the Russian National Revival Group. We will personally teach you how to survive and become an outstanding citizen of the Motherland once we return to the surface!"

Igor stared intently at the television. In the sunless environment of the bunker, opportunities for dozens of people to gather and watch even a short, simple broadcast were exceedingly rare. Igor had long since lost track of how long he had been underground. Since the cataclysmic Great Trial began, Igor, like most citizens, had been brought to this perpetually unchanging subterranean world. Here, the familiar sunlight was gone, the chirping of crickets was absent, leaving only the sight of other helpless people brought underground with him. The smile that once graced Igor's face was gone, replaced by an endless void.

"Hello, I am Grigori, a League Agricultural Professor. Today, I will lecture on how to carry out agricultural cultivation after we return to the surface. You must all know that the air on the surface is now filled with nuclear radiation." He pointed to the sky displayed on a nearby screen: "If our people go out unprotected, they will die quickly..."

Die? The word turned over in Igor's mind, stirring a memory. After arriving underground, continuous earthquakes had terrified everyone. But once the tremors stopped, some people stood up and protested, claiming the war was over and demanding the League let them go home. In response, the League had them all shot.

"...After the air settles, we will need to decontaminate the surface soil. Remember, do not plant seeds on the surface; the radiation will kill all unadapted seeds. To counter this, we have already cultivated some radiation-adapted seeds, and we will overcome the disaster as quickly as possible so you can all return to your work..."

Igor didn't clearly hear what was said next. He was fixated on the seeds, and memories surged from the depths of his mind. He used to be a farmer, working daily on the state farm. Harvest time was his happiest moment—the golden wheat, the corn, the cattle, and the dogs were his daily companions, an essential part of his past life.

When he finally snapped out of it, the broadcast had ended. Igor returned to his cramped dormitory, lay on his bed, and before closing his eyes, he made a note of the program's airtime.

title: New Cultural Standards
desc:
Underground, there is no concept of time like on the surface. As a result, most citizens and officials often collapse into bed after completing their mandated workload, conserving precious electricity for the League's continued existence. Today, however, a new meeting was underway in the Cultural Department's conference room.

"Take a look," Commissioner Sergei said with a smile, seated in the center of the Cultural Department's seats. On the table were several open books; some contained romantic tales, while others described a doctor's observations within the League. "Your work has been somewhat negligent. The Marshal Commander has issued an order to promote the excellent spiritual culture of the Russian people, and omissions like these can easily lead to complacency among our citizens."

"It is our oversight. Please forgive us," the Cultural Department officials bowed their heads. After a moment, Minister Fyodorov looked up, admitting the error in their work. "I will promptly correct these mistakes and confess my faults to the Marshal Commander."

"More than correcting mistakes, he desires a new standard," Sergei glanced at Fyodorov, then pulled a slip of paper from his pocket. "Your test has been passed. I hope you will correct these errors through your work and fulfill your duty to the revival of Russia."

After Fyodorov took the note and discussed it with the officials, a new prioritized cultural publication list was swiftly produced:

(1) Frontline Experiences: Focused descriptions of Russian soldiers' heroic deeds on the battlefield, their camaraderie, and war experiences of national pride and dying for the Motherland.
(2) Spiritual Interpretation: Propaganda for the heroic acts of Karbyshev and Marshal Commander Yazov, emphasizing loyalty to and support for the Great Trial.
(3) Local Customs: Archival and promotional records of Russian regional cultures and customs, ensuring the preservation of Russian national characteristics and traditional practices, and emphasizing the unity and coexistence of the Russian people.
(4) Anti-German Propaganda: Full-force reinforcement of hatred education against the dark history of Nazism, exposing and deepening a systematic explanation of the Teutonic people's national inferiority, and destroying the entire foundation of Nazi culture from scientific, racial, and various other perspectives.

After careful deliberation, Fyodorov added a final revision.

options.name: Aside from these standards, all other works will not be granted publication permits. Illegal printing will be immediately suppressed.

title: Bureaucratic Labor
desc:
Belyakov never liked dealing with common folk, neither at work nor outside of it. Over the years, he had one impression of them: ungrateful wretches. When it came to work, these people would bow lower than anyone and speak with the softest tones, but as soon as they left the job, they immediately forgot Belyakov's goodwill. Although Belyakov considered his temper to be quite good, encountering so many ungrateful wretches, he could only accept his bad luck.

The superiors recently issued another order: "Increase work efficiency, avoid spiritual corruption." To this end, they held meetings for three consecutive days, where the leaders prattled on about ensuring work quality, reading the works of the Marshal Commander and Commander Yevgeny, and so on. This talk might fool the young newcomers, but Belyakov summarized it in one sentence: overtime, and unpaid overtime at that.

Sure enough, something recently happened in Sector D of the bunker. A family had a death but didn't report it to the government, resulting in the air purification system for the entire residential area becoming overloaded. By the time the police kicked down the door, the system was already at its limit. For this, the superiors swiftly issued an order: all government personnel would be divided into teams and sent down to designated civilian communities to go door-to-door, standing guard, immediately cleaning up and reporting any issues that arise.

As for Belyakov, since he was older, the leaders, after a unanimous discussion, gave him a very easy job.

"How is the situation with the Sector D duty staff?"

"Reporting, Commander. All Sector D staff are present and accounted for, and firefighting work is proceeding in an orderly manner. Please rest assured!"

Waking up every day, sitting down, and reporting to his superiors every ten minutes on a work situation he knew nothing about—this was Belyakov's new job.

title: Elites? Cannon Fodder?
desc:
Galansha carried his tray and sat down in a corner. Just as he was about to eat, someone sat down across from him with a tray. He looked up and saw his old acquaintance, Burkin, a scout also in the Vympel unit. They exchanged a smile. As Galansha cut his bread, Burkin lowered his voice, "Brother, what have you guys been up to the past couple of days?"

Galansha's hand slowed. He quickly scanned the surroundings and replied quietly, "Engineering work. The superiors said we'd eventually return to the surface, so we need to prepare. What about you, brother? What's your unit been doing recently?"

"Ha, little brother, let me tell you. Five days ago, the brass sent me to a factory, saying there were rebels lurking, and I was supposed to catch them. I spent a whole day watching those mannequins on the assembly line and didn't find anyone who looked like they wanted to rebel. I wasted a day there and didn't even get a proper meal. When I went to find the factory director, guess what the guy was doing? Drinking cheap vodka!"

He shoved a small piece of synthetic meat into his mouth, chewing vigorously as he spoke: "Yesterday, the superiors ordered us to clear out a rebel stronghold. They said these guys were opposing the Marshal Commander and trying to sabotage the Russian revival, so I went. You won't believe it, when I got there, the whole unit consisted of several old men and two teenagers. *These* are the current Vympel forces?"

Galansha frowned. Burkin continued rambling: "It was a disaster. A few of us were assigned to a minefield at the front. Allegedly, the rebels had mined it in advance, and we were told to clear them. What the hell? Didn't the sappers or those Teuton trash used to do this kind of thing? The most damn annoying thing was that the guys in the squad acted like they hadn't had any training. One kid just walked straight onto a mine! Thankfully, I was quick enough to stop him from moving and then defused it, or else we'd all be feeding the lice." Galansha looked at his comrade, trying to find words to argue, but couldn't speak. He suddenly felt a genuine exhaustion, a profound emptiness creeping into his heart. Russia wasn't like this before, so why now...? Marshal Commander Yazov couldn't have made this mistake... but was this truly unrelated to the Marshal Commander? He shivered, casting these thoughts out of his mind.

options.name: "Brother, I'm a bit tired. I need to hurry back, have a couple of drinks, and go to bed."

title: Execution
desc:
A group of new recruits stood in a bare square, facing a line of prisoners in uniform. Since the emergence of resistance against the League, the Black League had been systematically sweeping previous underground hideouts, bringing out the rebels and executing them. An officer quietly approached the recruits, his eyes narrowed, staring into the multitude of eyes fixed on him. His gaze was sharp and profound. Whenever a recruit met his eyes for a few seconds, they would immediately look away, afraid to meet his stare.

"It is a great pleasure to see you here, defenders of the League!" the officer announced loudly, his voice echoing in the soldiers' ears. "I am Aleksandr Semyonov. I have reviewed your files. Before enlisting, you held various identities: farmers, workers, scum of the Motherland. By rights, you should all be at your posts, or shot."

"But!" his tone suddenly intensified, "Traitors have emerged in the Motherland! They attempt to overthrow the government, rambling about freedom and revolution! In reality, they are trying to stop the Russian people from completing the final Great Trial! They are the most hateful of all—Spiritual Teutons!"

"Therefore, to test your loyalty, I sincerely invite you to participate in the execution of these traitors." Semyonov ripped the hood off one of the prisoners. "Sir, do you still insist on opposing the Great Russian Revival Government?"

"You bastard! Just kill me! I will never serve this reactionary government..."

Semyonov ruthlessly covered the man's mouth, then raised a hand: "Execute." 'Bang, bang, bang,' a series of gunshots rang out, and the prisoners fell to the ground. Semyonov issued a second order: "Now, stab these wretches in the heart again, just in case they're faking death."

"Commander, is it not wrong to insult the dead? The Bishop taught us we should have some compassion.."

Semyonov drew his pistol and fired at the source of the voice, leaving a bloody mark on the recruits' memory: "The Marshal Commander taught me that loyalty to the Motherland is paramount. If someone obstructs the Motherland's revival for the sake of some so-called belief, then their existence is meaningless."

title: Eternal Death
desc:
The sun rose and set as usual, its light filtering through the scattered radiation-filled air and onto a patch of shade. Lister sat beneath a tree, squinting, enjoying this hard-won warmth. For him, no past ambition, however grand, was as valuable as simply living another day. Since the bombs fell, Lister's life had changed. His former German Fatherland had been incinerated in endless flames. Superiors, family, duty—everything had departed from him. As a survivor, all Lister could do was maintain the most basic existence with the few others who remained.

As the sun set, Lister stood up, slowly unbuttoned his coat, shook the dust from his clothes, and walked towards the distant estate. There, a few former Wehrmacht members had cleared and cultivated a small manor using found farming tools. Children studied and played in the yard, and the old comrades talked and reminisced about the good old days while tending to the fields.

He walked back into the courtyard and embraced his wife, Valentina. Memories had tormented him throughout countless days of hiding until he met her, Valentina, his beloved. She gave him a new, beautiful life: building their residence bit by bit on the ruins, sewing his clothes when he was injured, and the joy of finding food. He suddenly felt that the past didn't matter anymore; living out his life like this after despair and death was good enough.

"Boom!" A familiar sound reached Lister's ears. He struggled to recall what it was: a mortar. He instinctively wanted to run out of the estate, but the shells had already landed, and yellow smoke began to spread through the courtyard. All of Lister's emotions coalesced into a single, helpless sigh—what was meant to come, had come. He took Valentina's hand and quickly hid inside a room.

The sounds from the manor gradually faded. Smoke seeped through the door. Lister and Valentina exchanged a look, then embraced. These Germans had walked through darkness and death with resolve and determination, yet they did not receive heaven's favor. Destiny showed its immense ruthlessness at this moment. The German song of rebirth came to an abrupt end here.

options.name: Night fell, swallowing all life with it.

title: Last Chance
desc:
Yazov sat upright in the center of the command post, maintaining his usual rigid posture, awaiting the final response. There were always people who resisted stubbornly, but the Black League would always be the ultimate winner. He thought this to himself, but he no longer yelled or became furious as he once did. As the savior of all Russia, he had the duty to lead Russia and her people through the Great Trial. Although the reports suggested the resistance was gaining momentum, Russia had already sacrificed too much for the final victory—this was nothing.

"Ring-a-ling-a-ling..." The telephone finally rang. Yazov picked it up.

"Marshal Commander, I have reached the designated negotiation site and conducted talks with the so-called resistance forces. I have important news to relay. The resistance forces propose that if we can meet the following conditions, they will agree to lay down their arms: end Russia's military administration, elect a civilian government, ease regulations, and cease military dictatorship..." The seated officers' brows furrowed the more they listened, but Yazov suddenly chuckled: "These conditions are quite incredible. Did you inform them of Russia's current situation?"

"I did, Marshal Commander, but the leaders of the resistance said some nonsense, something about: 'Although life in Russia is difficult now, the current military administration has caused too many Russians who shouldn't have died to perish due to unjust distribution. What Russia needs now is fairness and development, and the so-called Great Trial should end. Furthermore...'" He swallowed hard. "Speak." "They said: 'If the Germans have truly been completely annihilated as the Marshal Commander claims, then what is our next step?'"

Yazov's smile vanished. He suddenly felt a wave of malevolence rush from his toes to the top of his head. He yelled into the mouthpiece: "Your mission is complete. Now we know: these people are beyond saving." He nearly smashed the receiver back onto the hook, then turned to the officers present: "Are our men in position?"

"Supplies for some regions are still en route. The main troop deployments are in place and ready to launch an attack at any moment." After a brief silence, an officer stood up and replied.

options.name: "Launch the attack immediately. Kill all these traitors."

title: Renewed Conflict
desc:
Grigori called out and lit a kerosene lamp. Immediately, a large group of shadows walked out of the darkness and joined his ranks. The clothes they wore were disparate, and their identities were each more complex than the last: there were soldiers with Soviet Union revolutionary medals, a worker missing an arm, and even a few holding a black, white, and yellow flag who stood at the tail end of the column. They marched noisily towards the designated location in the west. In a few minutes, they were to attack a Black League military camp.

A few minutes later, they arrived at the site. Grigori raised his binoculars for a look. Fortunately, the Black League soldiers were still sleeping. He gave the signal, and the attack immediately began. Several elite soldiers sneaked up on the camp guards. After a few slight sounds, two guards fell to the ground. 'Bang,' a gunshot sounded in the distance, and the camp began to stir.

"Shit, charge!" Grigori didn't hesitate, immediately yelling. A group of people grabbed their rifles and began firing, while others pulled out prepared Molotov cocktails and threw them into the camp. The Black League soldiers, after an initial panic, began to fight back. Some, under the command of their officers, quickly sought cover, and the seasoned soldiers also tried to illuminate the area and counterattack. But with the night growing darker and the surprise attack, the soldiers were still at a disadvantage.

Suddenly, dozens of bright lights tore through the pitch-black night. Grigori fixed his gaze on them; the lights came from glowing military caps, beneath which were the familiar gas masks—the main Black League force had arrived! Before the insurgents could react, a few muffled sounds came from the distance, followed by a series of explosions. Most of the insurgents panicked under this barrage. Some tried to drop their weapons and flee, but they quickly fell under the guns of the surrounding Black League soldiers.

Without a second thought, Grigori grabbed his gun and led the charge. He knew that the whole group had fallen into chaos, and if he didn't quickly organize an offensive, the Black League dogs would once again dominate them. After he led a fierce charge with a group of soldiers, the leading officer was killed, and the Black League garrison began to retreat. He raised his gun and shouted, "For Russia!"

Unfortunately, his opponent was thinking the same thing. A distant sentry pulled the bolt on his rifle, fired at the weapon-wielding Grigori, and hit him squarely in the chest.

The Cossack warrior suddenly lost all his strength. His body began to slide helplessly to one side. The shouts and cries of his comrades gradually faded from his sight, but in the last moment before death, he suddenly and truly felt what it meant to be alive.

options.name: Freedom is worth the sacrifice of every person.

title: A Breath of Fresh Air
desc:
Since the nuclear war began, 250541 has been confined to this facility. They call it a bunker, saying it is the seed of Russia's revival, the ultimate bulwark against the Germans. However, 250541 only feels it's a huge, stuffy cage. Still, if it really can be used to defeat those Germans, then staying here and enduring it is fine; after all, he's been in tougher places.

The facility trembles occasionally, and if you listen closely, you can hear muffled booming sounds. Days passed by with these sounds as their soundtrack. Frankly, 250541 didn't know how many days had passed. There was no calendar in the facility, and while the work here was somewhat easier than on the surface, it was enough to make one lose track of time and stop thinking too much. Maybe it was just a different place for work.

Every Sunday, 250541 had to go to the center to listen to the 'Black Hat' give a speech. They said it was to maintain the Russians' willpower and faith, but the Black Hat always talked about the same things—either how much damage their efforts were inflicting on the Germans, or how the facility would restore Russia's greatness in the future. 250541 was thoroughly bored of it.

This Sunday was different. The Black Hat didn't stand on the podium and rattle off the ear-callousing speeches of the past. He sat slumped in a corner chair, arms crossed, staring at a nervous-looking man in a white coat, as if trying to drill a hole through his chest with his gaze. The White Coat slowly walked onto the stage from the side, cleared his throat with his back to the audience, then took out a piece of paper, alternately looking at it and nervously glancing at the audience. Then he began: "Comrades, we are at the most glorious moment of the League! The revenge bombs we have forged are relentlessly blasting those German devils every single day. We will level their cities, and they, in turn, want to strike back at us. This is why we must stay here. And what bomb has such massive power? The bombs we and they possess are called nuclear bombs, and this kind of bomb..."

250541 didn't understand a single word of what the White Coat said next. But he did understand *that* was where the booming noises came from! The enemy was dropping bombs on them, and look, they had no idea they had already hidden in this huge hole!

Perhaps those booming sounds would stop tomorrow. Would that mean they had won? If that truly happened, he would definitely run back to the surface, hide in his old house in the woods, and drink all the liquor he had secretly stashed in one go. By then, since the Germans would have been taught their lesson, maybe the Black Hat would be happy and just leave him alone? Maybe they'd even have a celebration themselves? Maybe......

options.name: Thinking these thoughts, 250541 smiled and fell asleep.

title: Suffocation
desc:
Three days, 250541 counted, and he hadn't heard the booming sounds for three days. Since the White Coat's speech a few days ago, 250541 felt almost resurrected, constantly anticipating the moment the bombs outside would stop. Even his steps, as he daily moved things back and forth at Gate 6, became swifter.

'If I move a few more, will the day we return to the surface come a few days sooner?' Thinking this, the heavy boxes that made him sweat profusely every day seemed more agreeable, as if they contained some kind of treasure. But what was inside them? Why was there so much to move every day? 250541 hadn't considered this question, and he had long known that it was best not to overthink the League's affairs; just follow orders, why bother with the rest?

Four days passed, 250541 counted, and there was still no sound of bombs. Had the German bastards run out of bombs? Or had they already pulverized all their cities? Was the 'Great Trial' the Black Hat spoke of finally over? Were they going to let them go home? My old...

"Hey!" A yell snapped 250541 back to reality. "Stop daydreaming! Do you want to eat tonight?" 250541 again lifted the heavy box he had put down just a few seconds ago.

Today was the ninth day, tomorrow would be the tenth.

'Are they still not going to let us go back?' 250541 found it increasingly difficult to stop thinking about this. 'What exactly are these boxes for?'

"Hey, Aleksei, do you know what these boxes are for?" After moving a box to its destination again, 250541 asked his co-worker 250423. "I don't know. They just told me to drive all these to Gate 7." After speaking, 250423 glanced around, leaned in, and cautiously asked, "Don't overthink these things, you know that, right?" Whether he heard him or not, 250541 looked towards Gate 7, nodding vaguely.

On the tenth day, in front of Gate 7, 250541's heart pounded. He hid among the stack of boxes, watching the workers at Gate 7 come and go. The ceiling lights shone brightly, casting pitch-black shadows. 250541 regretted what he was doing. 'Bribing the foreman is a capital offense!' 250541 wiped the sweat from his brow. 'And the patrol could find him missing at any moment.' 'But, but, I've already come this far...'

250541 hastily tried to tear open a nearby box, but his hands were trembling uncontrollably. Then he heard someone nearby saying something: "These, you'll drive them directly to Gate 1 this time. 250876 can't drive, so you'll take the truck. Understand?" After hearing this, 250541 thought for a moment, startled, his eyes widened. He steeled his resolve and forcefully ripped open the box.

What was inside the box? Square, quite rough, and a little abrasive to the touch? 250541 was stunned.

It was a box of bricks.

The very bricks they had always been told were for rebuilding Russia on the surface.

250541 finally understood. There were seven gates. After Gate 7, the load naturally returned to Gate 1, then passed through the hands of a dozen people, and returned to Gate 6. This way, the work would never run out, and their 'willpower and faith' would never erode during their time underground.

Even after taking care of the Germans, the League would still be the League.

options.name: 250541 fell asleep. Tonight, he didn't overthink anything anymore.

title: Forbidden Book
desc:
Quiet, leisurely, comfortable. These words seemed irrelevant to the Black League, but since the nuclear war began, the bunker's radio had grown quieter day by day. Now, if you wanted to get any sound out of it, you'd probably have to kick it.

Thus, the radio operator, Rodion, found himself with rare free time. He forced himself not to think about the Black League and began reading a few books he had hastily brought down from the surface. Rodion didn't know what was in all of them, but one science fiction novel called 'The Heat Death' particularly captivated him.

In this book, humanity in the 2100s approached a unified communist society closer than ever before. Just as the prophesied utopia was about to be realized, it ultimately failed for various reasons, causing people to gradually doubt human nature. Amidst this doubt, a school of thought arose, claiming that Marx, centuries earlier, had not only constructed that future utopian society but had also inadvertently pointed out another possibility for the future: the complete collapse of human society.

The school claimed that the contradictions of human nature were unsolvable, and all social development merely used more complex social systems to temporarily mask these contradictions. When the complexity of society reached its limit, the previously concealed contradictions would erupt in a blowout, leading human society towards an inevitable and complete collapse, which they called the 'Heat Death of Civilization.'

To people who had just experienced a Great Collapse, this all seemed incredibly plausible. Nations across the world accepted this theory, and humanity's goal shifted from social development to preventing the total collapse of human society.

In the wreckage left by the Great Collapse, one could see various fantastic attempts to prevent the Heat Death of Civilization: there were anti-utopian societies practicing the annihilation of human emotion, transhumanists attempting to modify human nature, groups who outright abandoned modern society for primitive worship, and idealists who still believed in a unified communal society.

The one that caught Rodion's attention the most was an extremist organization. They claimed that human society was beyond saving, and they must destroy the current human society to rebuild a brand new one through their own hands. This extremist organization called itself the 'Cure for Humanity,' yet it practiced every form of terrorism and totalitarian rule imaginable, still justifying it as a necessary cleansing of humanity.

At the end of the novel, this extremist organization launched nuclear weapons globally. After the nuclear apocalypse, the survivors not only failed to follow the extremist organization's command to rebuild a new civilization but instead formed a united resistance army against them. Ultimately, human society met the 'Heat Death of Civilization' in an endless civil war.

Rodion closed the book and threw it into the trash.

title: The Kazakh Recruit
desc:
On the grayish-hued grassland, artillery boomed, and smoke and ash billowed. Inside a trench, a few people were huddled together, discussing something. "7524," the lieutenant called out, addressing the new recruits in front of him: "Agent 7524!" Yet, no one responded.

"Hey, Dmitry, he's calling you." Reznov nudged the distracted Dmitry next to him. "Oh, what is it? No, yes!" Dmitry startled, stammering his reply. The lieutenant frowned but let it go. All the newly conscripted soldiers were like this.

"We need to sneak over, blow up that machine gun bunker with explosives, and make no sound on the way." So, a few people stood up, hunched their backs, and slowly crept along the trench toward the machine gun bunker.

An unpleasant odor of unknown origin wafted through the trench. As Dmitry walked, he took out his canteen and gulped down the water. Ever since receiving his conscription notice, he had been depressed, and it wasn't entirely because he didn't want to go to the front. When Dmitry was 12, his mother was killed by a German bomber. Since then, he had worked tirelessly in the factory for the Great Trial. But now, they weren't fighting Germans at all. Dmitry was conscripted to kill his own countrymen. Looking at the people in the distant machine gun bunker, their relatives were probably killed by the Germans too, right? Thinking this, Dmitry sighed inwardly and twisted the cap back on.

Just then, a 'bang' came from a distance. A black speck dropped from the pale sky and landed abruptly next to Reznov. Flames instantly engulfed, consumed, and then spat him out. The half-charred Reznov heavily slammed down next to Dmitry. *Thud*. Dmitry looked down; Reznov's black, scorched corpse lay quietly by his feet, accompanied only by a faint sizzling sound. The canteen in his hand slipped, hitting the ground with another *thud*. Dmitry was stunned for a few seconds, his vision blurred, his legs went weak, and then he screamed in terror.

"7524, shut up! You're going to expose us!" the lieutenant said impatiently. But Dmitry didn't respond, continuing to scream. Reznov was the only friend he had known at the factory. How could this have happened?

"7524!" The lieutenant leaned in and shoved Dmitry hard, but he was still engulfed in his emotions, continuing to yell. "The new recruits are all like this." The lieutenant habitually drew his small knife and, without hesitation, sliced across Dmitry's neck as cleanly as cutting pork. Blood instantly spurted out, splashing onto the empty canteen. Dmitry gurgled, falling next to Reznov. A few seconds later, he made no further sound.

title: White Noise
desc:
*buzz buzz buzz...*

The alarm dragged A out of his deep sleep. A rubbed his tired eyelids, slowly sat up, leaning on the bed, staring blankly at the foot of the bed for a few seconds. Then, he got off barefoot and walked a few steps towards the locker. Opening the locker, A realized he was already wearing his work uniform. He hurriedly put on his shoes, grabbed yesterday's leftover dry bread, and quickly walked out of the dormitory.

*Bang, bang, bang, bang*. Four sounds; one workpiece was finished. 'During training, the instructor always said to be extremely careful when machining this part, but after getting used to it, it's the same routine over and over.' Thinking this, A wiped a large bead of sweat from his forehead with his hand, flicked it to the side, and finally wiped his hand on the blackened thigh side of his pants. Just then, the next workpiece arrived, followed by another *bang, bang, bang, bang*.

*Ding ding ding ding...*

Not long after the last workpiece was finished, the meal bell rang. A unhurriedly put down his tools, stretched his exhausted arms a few times, and walked toward the mess hall. Today's meal was the same indescribable food. He swallowed it with the semi-stale bread; it still didn't taste very good. Bite after bite, accompanied by the factory's rumbling roar, A finished the last piece of bread.

*Ding ding ding ding...* Right on cue, the work-call bell rang. A stood up and walked back to the factory.

*Bang, bang, bang, bang...* A smoothly finished several more workpieces. 'It's all the same routine. It's not as careful as the instructor said it needed to be.' A thought, casually wiped the sweat from his forehead, flicked it hard to the side, and finally wiped it on the blackened patch on his pants' thigh. Just then, the next workpiece arrived.

*Ding ding ding ding...* It was time for dinner. A rushed to the mess hall as usual, eating dinner quickly, leaving only one piece of bread for the next day's breakfast. He then rushed back to the factory. The evening shift always felt so rushed.

*Bang, bang, bang, bang...*

Workpiece after workpiece went by. Staring at the next one, A began to think again: 'The instructor said to be very careful when machining these parts, but after getting used to it, it's essentially the same routine.' After thinking this, A wiped the sweat from his forehead, flicked it to the side, and finally wiped it on the thigh of his pants—*rip*, the pants tore.

"Ah!"

A's hand froze. He glanced at his pants, then sharply looked up, suddenly seeing all the workers around him performing the exact same motions. Their faces were all washed out by the harsh white light, blending into a single mass. In their hands, the loud *bang, bang, bang, bang* sounds continued. Identical workpieces moved past, one after another. Looking around, the massive factory was unnaturally spacious, yet he felt a suffocating crowd. The continuous *bang* and *rumble* sounds from all directions immediately pressed down on him, as if four gigantic walls were pushing, about to crush him to death. But in just two or three seconds, the workpiece he had been staring at passed by. Snapping out of it, A frantically grabbed his tools and turned back to work.

*Ring ring ring...* The quitting time bell rang.

A shuffled his feet toward the employee dormitory, pushed open the door, tossed the dry bread onto the table, and, as if drained, fell straight onto the bed.

options.name: He forgot to take off his work uniform again.

title: The Dark Cloud
desc:
Under the cloud-covered sky was a boundless snowscape, with a distant horizon separating gray and white, like two strokes of paint on an oil canvas. In the center of the snowfield, a few twisted wooden huts emerged sparsely from the ground—this was where the nuclear-radiation-fleeing vagrants had sought refuge.

The village had no name. The vagrants built shelters, forged tools, and cultivated fields, but they never named the village.

The sun had just risen in the murky sky, and a grayish haze lingered in the air beneath the clouds. The hunter who lived at the edge of the village grabbed his bow, took a swig from his canteen of liquor, pushed open his door, and went out hunting. Before long, the children in the village ran to the hunter's doorstep to play. The largest, darkest, and thinnest child chased the others, but stopped after a few steps, squatting listlessly and staring blankly at the distant trees. The other children, seeing he was no longer chasing them, played with snow piles where they stood, but soon grew bored and dispersed.

Just after noon, the farmers set up their stalls in the center of the village. Under a makeshift canopy made of rags, a farmer with cracked skin sat in front of his stall, idly looking at the few potatoes spread on the table. "How much for this?"

Hearing the visitor, the farmer slowly looked up, opened his dry mouth, and spoke in a hoarse voice: "One bullet for five."

"I'll buy five."

Taking the bullets and placing them in a rusty can, the farmer lowered his head and continued looking at the potatoes.

In the afternoon, the village's only doctor sat at a table with a pen, the tip pressed against his notebook, but unmoving. These were his last few pages. Since the flight, patients came daily, and the pages of his notebook were quickly used up, yet he remained stubborn about recording their symptoms. Gazing at the few pages remaining, the doctor wanted to write something—he wanted to record everything that had happened in the land once called 'Russia' over the past forty years, or perhaps the various city ruins along the migration route, or even just jot down an interesting anecdote from last month... "Doctor, I don't feel well."

The doctor dismissed his wandering thoughts, looked at the incoming patient, asked about the symptoms in detail, and recorded them on the few remaining pages.

Soon after, the sun was about to set, and the hunter arrived home with his catch. Opening the wooden door, his wife's cooked meal was on the table, emitting a fragrant aroma. The hunter, who had been hungry for half a day, placed the wild boar he was carrying by the wall and sat at the table to feast.

"You're back?"

"Mhm."

"Good that you're back."

"Mhm. Caught a boar."

"Dinner's ready."

"Mhm."

After dinner, the hunter lay on the bed, looking at the night view outside the window, thinking about tomorrow's matters. Thinking and thinking, he fell asleep.

Finally, the sun fully set. The last ray of sunlight vanished, and the dark clouds covered the sky, blending into the night. On one side, the moon slowly rose. A faint moonlight shone through the clouds onto the snowfield, like a streak of blue on a black canvas.

options.name: Perhaps one day, the dark cloud will finally disperse.

title: The Number
desc:
Agent 181410 was driving through the mountains and forests when the Great Trial began. It wasn't until countless nuclear weapons streaked across the sky, flying west, that he realized the Great Trial had started. He immediately had to take refuge in an abandoned bunker by the roadside. After hiding for a day and a night, 181410 felt no activity, so he left the bunker. The sky was pitch black, but the carnage 181410 had envisioned—like a German counterattack or bombing—had not occurred. 'Perhaps it's because our Great Trial was well-prepared and completely vanquished the Teutonic barbarians, giving them no chance to strike back,' he thought to himself. Then, 181410 found the car he had hastily parked on the side of the road earlier. It still ran, so 181410 drove away.

The sky remained murky. Beneath it, the ecstatic 181410 drove on. He drove crookedly, like a drunkard behind the wheel. "We did it, yes, we did it! The Marshal Commander must have succeeded. Mother Russia has finally defeated the Teutonic barbarians, and the Motherland will prosper!" He shouted deliriously. "I told you, Commander Yazov's Three Great Theories are the absolute truth! Long live the Marshal Commander! The Great Trial has finally arrived, and the humiliation and suffering our Mother Russia endured are finally over! We have truly avenged the Motherland; the inferior Teutonic barbarians are all dead! Hahahahaha!" The more 181410 thought about it, the more excited he became, even starting to laugh hysterically. "What should I do next? After completing the Great Trial, after achieving vengeance against the Teutons, what is my purpose?"

Suddenly, a series of questions filled 181410's mind. It was true: after planning the Great Trial for so many years, 181410 had never considered what he would do once it was over. With the completion of this goal, 181410's heart was seized by an unprecedented emptiness. Just then, he saw a glimmer of light on the horizon, pointing east, the direction of his hometown. No doubt, that light must be the rising sun. He immediately turned the car around, racing towards the newborn sun, towards his hometown, to tell the folks in his town that the Great Trial was successful and the Russian nation had risen!

options.name: "Glory to you, my Russia. Glory to you, my Marshal Commander!"

title: Rebirth
desc:
Then, he had a thought. "Oh, right, I should devote myself to building Mother Russia. Yes, yes! After such a brutal war, the Motherland must begin reconstruction, and I will be the builder who rebuilds the Motherland and makes it prosperous and strong!" Thinking this, 181410 felt completely satisfied. "So, how should the reborn Russia be built? What was that city the Teutons were most proud of called? Let me think. Oh right, Germania. Yes, that's what it was called. From now on, even the most remote small town in Russia must be better, bigger, and more luxurious than Germania! Yes, that's how it must be! And our capital should be more magnificent and spectacular than Tokyo and Washington combined! I must build the Motherland to be like this!" 181410 chirped happily, driving toward the light in the east that represented his hometown. "Wait, could Commander Yazov have died in the nuclear blast? If he died, who will lead us? No, absolutely not! Omsk has the strongest bunker. The Marshal Commander will definitely survive... *click... click... click...*" As he drove toward the light, 181410 suddenly heard a strange series of clicking sounds. He stopped and rummaged through the clutter in the car to find the source of the noise.

Suddenly, he froze, his hand trembling as it gripped the source of the clicking—a Geiger counter. "Wait, why is there still nuclear radiation here?" Just as he was puzzled, a purplish-red sunset appeared in the western sky, piercing through the black smoke and revealing the azure sky. Illuminated by the sun's light, 181410 finally saw clearly: his former hometown had become a ruin engulfed in a sea of fire. Its desolation was far more severe than any German atrocity 181410 had ever heard of. A strong gust of wind blew, extinguishing the sparks in the sea of fire and blowing out 181410's sanity.

options.name: Why is this happening? The Great Trial was successful...

title: Sin
desc: *Click... click... click...* The Geiger counter continued its liberal clicking. 181410 painfully pressed his head against the steering wheel, trying not to look at the misery before him. "Why, why is this happening! The first trial didn't destroy my hometown, the second one didn't, and even the Great Trial didn't. But now, it's completely a ruin! Wasn't the Great Trial over? Wasn't the Russian nation supposed to be revived? What the hell kind of revival is this?!" 181410's eyes were red, and a few drops of murky tears fell. Thinking of how he had just been planning how to build a better Russia, he suddenly felt ridiculous. "What the hell is the Great Trial, and the Marshal Commander? It's all nonsense! Yes, that's right. Yazov is a beast in human form, a grand deceiver who fooled the Russian people, binding them to his perverse hatred for the Germans, ultimately causing our Mother Russia to suffer such great hardship! Furthermore, if even a town like my hometown has been destroyed, what about all of Mother Russia...?" Thinking this, 181410 felt a chill that erupted from his very bones. "No Russian demanded vengeance against Germany. No one wanted to fight anymore. Yet, that animal Yazov used the so-called Three Great Theories to constantly deceive Russians into going to the battlefield to slaughter and realize his own ambitions, his own delusions! Yazov is the true traitor to Mother Russia!" Thinking this, the fury in 181410's eyes matched the sea of fire before him.

options.name: "To hell with the number 181410! My real name is..."

title: The Steppe
desc:
Mikhail drove fast and aimlessly across the endless Russian steppe. He had once been drawn in by the Three Great Theories, believing the Great Trial was everything in his life.

But now, everything had changed. However, Mikhail had invested so much into the Great Trial that he only remembered himself as Agent 181410 and had forgotten his own name.

Mikhail drove to a high vantage point. He looked up, gazing into the distance. The cities in the distance were all shrouded in thick smoke and filled with wailing, yet Mikhail's memory told him these were places that had escaped the ravages of the war decades ago and had developed peacefully. But now, under the rule of that vengeance-crazed lunatic Yazov, they had also been reduced to this state. Thinking this, Mikhail clenched his jaw, his fingernails digging into his palm.

He hated. He hated Yazov, that grand deceiver who had plunged Russia into suffering once again. He hated himself for so easily believing Yazov's lies and felt ashamed of his earlier fantasies about a bright future... He turned his head and saw the boundless steppe. The azure sky pierced through the rolling black smoke. The grass and trees on the ground swayed gently with the breeze. With things as they were, Mikhail could only stand on these ruins, bathed in the solitary evening wind.

Suddenly, he felt that the endless steppe before him was incredibly beautiful. He finally remembered his name. He was Mikhail Yuryevich, named after a jewel in the crown of Russian culture. He realized that for so many years, he had been obsessed with the ridiculous Great Trial, and this was the first time he had wholeheartedly gazed upon the magnificent steppe of Russia. Amidst the vast and distant sky and earth, Mikhail was finally free from years of fanaticism and felt an inner peace. He walked on the Russian steppe, feeling the fragrance of the soil and its wondrous texture. 'I love this land,' he thought joyfully. All the fervor, all the anger, all the resentment, and regret disappeared, leaving only love for this steppe. Gradually, Mikhail walked further away, his sturdy figure slowly becoming a blurred black speck, disappearing into the vast land.

options.name: “It is not seeking happiness, nor fleeing it in haste!”

title: The Hermit
desc:
A young agent stood holding his breath in front of a broken wooden door. He knocked first, but there was no sound from inside, no sign of life. So, he took out the file given to him by the Reconstruction Bureau.

According to the file, this area was not a target during the nuclear war, and one of the Black League's top agents happened to be operating in the area, meaning he had a high probability of surviving the nuclear war. Furthermore, according to nearby villagers, a suspicious man was indeed lodging here.

"From the archives, he truly is a fine comrade of mine! This comrade outstandingly completed so many missions and was extremely devoted to both the Great Trial and the Marshal Commander. This is the example we should follow; he is a model for our generation!" he thought to himself, reviewing the archive.

The young agent's thoughts returned to the present. Facing the silent wooden door, the young agent decided to lean back, then violently kicked out one leg, driving his thick heel into the old door lock. Due to the immense impact, the wooden door finally rattled and shook open.

What met his eyes was a solemn man dressed in a black robe. He was quietly reading a book that was not particularly thick. Seeing the visitor, the man gently placed the book face-up on a nearby table, and his soft gaze fixed on the eyes of the uninvited guest.

"You are Agent—Number 181410, right?" the young agent asked directly.

"I was 181410, but now, I am only Mikhail Yuryevich. The 181410 you are looking for is not here. Please leave!"

The young agent suddenly picked up a wooden plank nearby and swung it toward Mikhail's head. Mikhail lightly raised his hand and caught the plank flying towards his head with one hand. "Still sharp, old comrade! Come back with me. The Black League has been rebuilt under the leadership of Marshal Commander Yazov. We are short-handed now." Hearing the names Yazov and the Black League, a strange look flashed across Mikhail's face, but it was quickly replaced by a look of composure.

options.name: "Come on, come back with me and fight for the Black League, for Mother Russia, for Commander Yazov!"

title: Reincarnation
desc:
The young agent extended a friendly hand to Mikhail, inviting him to leave with him. Mikhail suddenly tilted his head, standing stiffly, as if contemplating some complex, unspeakable secret. Just as the young agent was puzzled, Mikhail slowly stood up, and the smile on the young agent's face grew brighter.

Mikhail followed the young agent out of the hut and into the yard. At this point, Mikhail straightened his posture and solemnly said to the young agent: "I will no longer serve or work for the Black League or Yazov. I will only serve Mother Russia." Hearing this, the young agent replied with a slight chuckle, "The Black League and Marshal Commander Yazov are the embodiment of our Mother Russia! Only the Black League and Marshal Commander Yazov can protect and nurture our Motherland! Senior, you must be confused. Have you forgotten even this?"

"No, you are wrong. Yazov or the Black League are not, and can never be, the representatives of Mother Russia. Yazov is a maniac, a lunatic, a grand deceiver! To achieve his so-called vengeance ideal, he would even let Russia be destroyed along with it! He fooled everyone and enslaved all the Russian people to achieve his perverse goals!" Hearing this, the young agent's eyes darkened, and his initial enthusiasm was extinguished. "So, that's how it is," he muttered to himself. "I see! I see! I understand everything!" Seeing the young agent's look of sudden understanding, Mikhail felt a sense of relief.

"It's not too late for you to make a different choice," Mikhail said sincerely. "I understand completely now. The reason the Great Trial was not entirely successful, why the Teutonic barbarians still exist, and why Mother Russia suffers at their hands, is because of faithless traitors like you!" the young agent roared, then drew the pistol from his waist.

title: Duel
desc:
Years of life on the steppe had not dulled Mikhail's skills; rather, his senses had become sharper. Just as the young agent prepared to draw and shoot, Mikhail threw the wooden plank in his hand, striking the agent's hand and knocking his pistol away. The dark iron-colored handgun fell about five meters behind the agent. Mikhail then drew his own pistol from his waist with lightning speed. Looking at the dark muzzle pointed at him, the young agent closed his eyes, but still cursed Mikhail as a traitor under his breath.

"Let us settle this the Russian way," Mikhail said calmly. "Let's end our dispute with the most traditional game." With that, Mikhail also threw his gun about five meters behind him. The young agent was stunned for a second by the sight, then instantly turned and sprinted forward to grab his gun. Mikhail's reflexes were still superior. Just as the agent grabbed his gun, he heard the crisp click of Mikhail engaging his gun's safety. Having no other choice, he shoved the muzzle out from under his armpit on the other side of his body and expertly blind-fired behind him. Ultimately, the young agent knew he was a step too late. Before he could pull the trigger, he had already heard the *click* of Mikhail's pistol trigger, followed by a loud bang, and then...

options.name: Two gunshots—one after the other—pierced the silence of the steppe.

title: The End
desc:
When the young agent looked back, he saw that Mikhail had raised his arm straight up and fired a shot into the sky, while his own shot had squarely hit Mikhail's heart. The young agent's marksmanship was indeed excellent. Mikhail was killed instantly.

The young agent looked at Mikhail's corpse before him and felt a sudden sadness. He couldn't understand why the Black League's once most outstanding warrior had fallen to this state. His number, 181410, had represented so much honor, so much glory, and was so admirable, yet he had met such an end. It was truly regrettable.

What puzzled the young agent even more was that Mikhail clearly had the chance to kill him, but instead fired wildly into the sky. "What a lunatic," the young agent sighed with emotion. "And those bizarre ravings—only a lunatic like that could utter them."

Then, the young agent moved Mikhail's body into the wooden hut and retrieved his gun. It was then that the young agent noticed the book Mikhail had been reading when he burst through the door, which was now lying open on the table. As if drawn by the book's gravity, the agent's curiosity was piqued. The young agent picked up the book and began to examine it closely.

The book was old and thin. The pages were yellowed but intact; every page was complete. Judging by the year, it must have been produced during the Tsarist era. The cover was embellished with gilded edges. The author was already blurred and illegible, but the title remained clear, printed in blood-red ink in a script font—*The Demon*.

options.name: "Let me see the page 181410 was just reading."

title: The Demon
desc:
...The melancholic Demon, the banished spirit,
Hovering over the sin-steeped Earth,
The scenes of his beautiful past years,
Appeared one after another before him:
He recalled when, as a pure Seraph,
He brilliantly displayed his talents in the bright abode;
He recalled when the swift-racing comet,
Often returned his smile with an affectionate smile,
To signify a greeting;
He recalled when, with a thirst for knowledge,
He peered through the perpetual mist,
Looking down at the swarms of floating, God-abandoned stars;
He recalled when, as a favorite of creation,
He kept hope and was full of love!
He never doubted, nor felt hate,
The centuries of useless and tedious time,
Had not affected the purity of his soul...
And much, much more... but to recall all this
Was now beyond his strength!

options.name:
"And it wildly prayed for the storm,
As if only in the storm lay peace!"

title: Excising the Decay
desc:
Marshal Commander Yazov's voice was as fierce and merciless as the north wind, penetrating every crevice of the bunker. His eyes, filled with the fire of vengeance, swept across the war room, finally resting on the banners symbolizing loyalty and dedication. Yet, in his eyes, an unseen decay was breeding beneath those banners. At this moment of life and death for the Great Trial, any trace of betrayal or weakness was an unforgivable crime.

"We will rebuild our home on the ruins of the nuclear war," Yazov's voice was low and powerful, "and for that, we need to endure the trials of hunger and chaos. But now, some thieves are exploiting their official positions to steal the Federation's precious supplies. They think they've gotten away with something, but they cannot escape the eyes of the League."

As the order was given, the atmosphere in the bunker immediately tightened. Agents known as 'Executioners' moved like ghosts through the corridors. Their targets were comprehensive: dissenting officers, officials whose dedication to the cause of vengeance had wavered, and anyone deemed a potential destabilizing factor. Concurrently, the League issued a public notice, promising rewards for verified reports of suspected corruption.

A young officer named Sergei Ivanov was taken away for privately complaining about food rations. He insisted his remarks were not malicious, only intended to improve the soldiers' lives. However, in the eyes of the 'Executioners,' this was merely an excuse for weakness and wavering. Another elderly engineer was scrutinized for insisting that a certain biological weapon research project was too wasteful. He tried to argue with data and theories, but his words were powerless before the Great Trial. In Yazov's creed, any sacrifice was necessary for the Great Trial, even those who had contributed to the League.

As the purge deepened, the bunker became quieter, but this silence did not stem from peace; it sprang from fear. Everyone was careful about their words and actions, afraid of becoming the next target to be 'excised.' Yet, within this atmosphere of dread, Yazov saw the purity he desired: a League utterly loyal to the cause of vengeance, free of any dissonance. He firmly believed that only this could ensure Russia's victory in the final 'Great Trial'.

options.name: This purge will ensure our will is one.

title: Purging the Vermin
desc:
“Decay does not exist merely on the level of thought; it also manifests as the filthy form of greed and laziness, entrenched deep within the very strongholds upon which we depend for survival."
Generalissimo Yazov's voice echoed in every corner of the bunker. Following the previous purge of ideological disloyalty, he turned his attention to another equally fatal enemy: bureaucratic corruption. In this crisis of life and death, the officials responsible for allocating supplies and managing industry had turned their power into a tool for self-enrichment. Food rations were withheld, weapon parts were sold on the black market, and crucial industrial plans stalled. These actions were like a fatal tumor, eroding the very foundations of the Black League's survival.
The purge immediately commenced. This time, the executioners' targets were not only ideologically impure intellectuals or wavering officers but also those glamorous officials with hands stained by ill-gotten gains.
A logistics official named Grigory was arrested publicly. He was accused of hoarding vast quantities of scarce canned food and medicine and trading them privately on the black market. Crates of contraband were discovered in his home—supplies that could have saved the lives of countless soldiers and workers. In the tribunal, he attempted to defend his actions, but his voice was quickly drowned out by the roar of angry citizens and officers.
Another engineer, responsible for weapons production, was arrested for inflating production data and profiting from it. His reports listed countless guns and shells that should have been produced, but in reality, these items did not exist. In his factory, many workers were idle due to a lack of essential tools and raw materials, and production had ground to a halt. His execution order was delivered within a day, making him the first typical case of a corrupt official within the bunker.
"These vermin are more terrifying than German bombs," Yazov said in a subsequent broadcast. "They corrupt our souls. They steal the soldier's rations, they delay the production of weapons, and they defile the great cause we fight for with their self-interest."
The purge's effect was immediate. After a brief period of chaos, order in the bunker became more stable. Generalissimo Yazov looked at the submitted trial reports, his face expressionless. He believed that, for the sake of a pure and powerful Russia, any obstacle must be ruthlessly swept aside.

options.name: The Great Trial requires everyone to fulfill their duties.

title: The Silent Wasteland
desc:
The bunker's gigantic blast doors slowly opened with a heavy mechanical groan. A long-lost beam of light, carrying a faint trace of fallout dust, fell upon the bunker's cold entrance. Since the endless inferno drove humanity underground, this door had been sealed for an untold number of years. Now, the surface radiation levels had finally dropped to an acceptable range. Under Generalissimo Yazov's command, the first teams to return to the surface, composed of the most elite reclaimers, were preparing to step onto this unfamiliar homeland.

Each of them was equipped with simple anti-radiation suits and tools, but their hearts were filled with complex emotions. Most of them had only ever seen blue skies, white clouds, and vast plains in textbooks and the memories of the older generation. Now, what lay before them was a desolate and lifeless wasteland. The once-prosperous city of Omsk was reduced to ruins; twisted steel skeletons and charred rubble were the only urban relics. There was no sound of wind, no birdsong, only the crunch of gravel beneath their feet. This shocking silence was more penetrating than the most terrifying nuclear blast—it spoke volumes of the end of an era.

A young reclaimer named Ivan Petrov discovered a rusted children's toy car among the ruins. He gently picked it up and wiped the dust off with his sleeve, as if he could see the past world full of laughter through it. A flash of sorrow crossed his eyes, but it was quickly replaced by a resolute determination. This destroyed world was precisely the vision of what 'The Great Trial' they fought for was meant to prevent. They had to act to make the Motherland rise from the ashes.

As planned, they established the first checkpoint within Omsk city, not only to monitor radiation levels but also to declare the Black League's absolute sovereignty over this land. The work of rebuilding houses proceeded simultaneously. Using salvaged industrial equipment and reclaimed metal, they began repairing residences. All work was unfolding in an orderly fashion so that more people could resume normal production and life.

"We shall re-tame this wasteland," the commander of the operation wrote in his report to the Generalissimo. "We will rebuild the Russian homeland with our sweat and will. We will establish a state composed entirely of strength, industry, and martial spirit. Russia shall become a beacon of justice and civilization, illuminating this world polluted by corrupted Nazi ideology."

That night, Ivan Petrov wrote in his diary: "Today, I touched the wreckage of the old world. It was not as vibrant as in the textbooks; it is merely a ruin now. I wonder if our 'Great Trial' is precisely to ensure that this silence never falls upon the Motherland's soil again."

options.name: The Old World is gone; a new world shall be reborn.

title: A Map of Hell
desc:
Looking at the distorted images on the screen, an unprecedented sense of emptiness and unease filled his heart. He had envisioned that civilizations in other regions had long been destroyed, but the reports from the front lines were vastly different from his expectations.

"Comrade Generalissimo," a signaler reported, "we detected Teutonic signals at Observation Point 7... not old ones, but currently in use."

This news was like a sharp dagger thrust into Yazov's beliefs. He had thought that all Teutonic remnants had been reduced to ashes in the nuclear baptism. But intelligence showed that Teutonic forces had survived. They were not consumed by the hell he himself had unleashed; instead, they had established a new order. On their homeland, like stubborn weeds, they were still fighting for survival. This was undoubtedly a mockery of Yazov's conviction and a merciless negation of the Great Trial's perfect conclusion. Everything he had planned day and night, the result for which countless Russians had sacrificed, turned out to be merely a fantasy.

Even more shocking was the second report from the reconnaissance team. Near the Ural Mountains, radio signals from multiple armed factions were detected. According to intelligence analysis, these forces were not the unified 'Black League' but various rebel factions. The Bolsheviks and liberal remnants he had purged and eliminated had actually survived; they had seized the strongholds established by the League and formed new organizations. Their flags bore no League symbol, only the negation of 'The Great Trial.' They had once been an internal problem for the League, but now they had become a massive external threat.

Yazov felt an emptiness he had never known. He had thought he was the architect of the final revenge, only to discover he was merely the originator of chaos. He had personally brought forth Hell, but this Hell was more complex and tumultuous than he had imagined. His 'Great Trial' had not ended everything; it had created a new world that was more bloody and cruel. This sense of nihilism was slowly devouring him. His faith, his goal, his entire life, all seemed to have lost its meaning.

options.name: For Russia, I must defeat them a second time!

title: Echoes from All Sides
desc:
In the bunker's communications room, the ticking of the telegraph machine became the sole main theme. Yazov stood before a massive operational map, his eyes fixed on the markers representing troops and strongholds. He had pulled himself out of the previous nihilism, pouring all his energy into a new 'Great Trial' strategy. The remnants of the old world sought a resurgence, but he would destroy them once again.

According to the Central League's assessment, despite the League's heavy losses, as long as they could reconsolidate the scattered League units, they still possessed enough power to crush everything. Whether it was the struggling Teutonic barbarians or the reactionary forces and bandits on Russian soil, all would be trampled underfoot.

Yazov issued the most urgent order: send telegrams to all known military districts and partisan groups, demanding their return to the fold. The wording of the telegram was filled with Yazov's characteristic coldness and resolve: 'Annihilate all banditry, and utterly reduce the Teutonic concept to history.'

One telegram was sent to the Far Eastern Military District, addressed to Colonel Pikalov. His troops were near Lake Baikal. Yazov believed Pikalov's loyalty and tenacity were sufficient to overcome all difficulties. The telegram promised that once he integrated the Far Eastern resources, the League would dispatch elite forces to support him.

Another telegram was sent to Alexander Lazarenko, the commander in the Ural Mountains. He had once been considered a 'waverer' for questioning the ideology of 'The Great Trial,' but he and his troops remained the elite core of the League. Yazov's telegram did not mention past grievances, simply stating the facts: only by uniting could they completely eliminate the enemy.

However, the telegraph responses were not all positive. Some telegrams vanished without a trace, indicating that some units might have been annihilated in the chaos or chosen to become independent. Other replies were full of doubt and distrust. They questioned whether Yazov's 'Great Trial' had truly brought victory, or merely more confusion.

Despite this, Yazov did not waver. He knew that the path to unifying Russia would always be accompanied by suspicion and betrayal. But as long as he could regroup those genuinely loyal to the cause of vengeance, his 'Great Trial' still had a chance of completion.

options.name: Issue a call to all regions, regardless of their past loyalty.

title: Steel and Glory
desc:
"To the Generalissimo, my unit has completed control of Krasnoyarsk and is ready to sweep the surrounding areas at any time..."

On the screen of the communications room, a long-awaited response finally appeared. The telegram came from **Krasnoyarsk**, a strategic location that had been isolated by the surface chaos. The dispatch was signed by **Alexander Sakharovsky**, the reformist leader who had been wholeheartedly aligned with the Generalissimo and had made great contributions to the Black League during the Great Trial. His troops had been garrisoned in this metallurgical and railway hub. When the Great Trial arrived, the local bunker system functioned excellently, preserving a large amount of precious industry, manpower, and supplies for the League.

Yazov's face showed no emotion, but a ripple flashed in his eyes. In the face of the fractured reality, this reply from an old comrade was undoubtedly a light in the darkness. Sakharovsky's telegram was concise and powerful. He reported the situation in Krasnoyarsk: the bunker system had survived the nuclear war, industrial facilities were preserved, and the local League forces had stabilized their position under his command. However, he did not mention external exploration, only emphasizing that after a long period of recuperation, they were now re-equipped with the capacity for effective local governance.

This telegram was of great significance. Strategically, it meant the Black League had gained massive support from the rear. Krasnoyarsk, as a vital industrial and resource center with abundant manpower and coal resources, would provide crucial support for the second phase of 'The Great Trial.'

But on a personal level, this telegram also brought complex emotions to Yazov. He had personally brought Hell to Russia, witnessing too many people degenerate and go mad in the silent solitude, yet there were still people like Sakharovsky upholding the League's original ideals. They had not been misled by the surface chaos and still adhered to the ideal of the Great Trial. Their existence was a silent affirmation of Yazov's path of vengeance.

However, Yazov also knew that consolidating Sakharovsky's forces would not be simple. This telegram was the beginning of cooperation, but it would also bring a lot of trouble to his old friend. He needed to unite all those loyal to the Great Trial, not create more problems for them. How to best utilize the strength of the various bunkers would be a challenge Yazov must face in the journey ahead.

options.name: Contact Sakharovsky again to discuss the rebuilding of the Eastern Front.

title: The Choice
desc:
It was the sixth day since the troops departed. Yazov tossed and turned in the officers' command post and began reviewing the dispatch reports of the various external liaison teams. He meticulously read the movement requests and reports from teams sent in all directions, wrote down his instructions, opened a drawer, and placed them in pre-prepared folders, from which the staff would forward them for execution. The folder for exploration instructions around Omsk was already full, and the folder for the westward teams also contained many documents. Only the folder for the teams sent to the East remained empty.

He sighed, about to return to the general command to continue the meeting, when the signaler next to him suddenly gasped and began operating the black-and-white typewriter in front of him. Yazov quietly watched the young soldier gradually translate the telegram. Soon, the clacking of the typewriter stopped, and a complete survey report was handed to Yazov.

**To the Generalissimo: Regarding the Status and Challenges of Our 'Westward' Movement**

Since our unit departed eastward, aside from encountering numerous destroyed facilities along the way, multiple factions have launched attacks against us. According to our reconnaissance, these factions are mostly bandits who emerged in various settlements after the Great Trial, but there are also small loyal League units fighting them, to whom we have provided sufficient weapons, ammunition, and communication facilities for contact.

Our vanguard has reached **Kyzyl**. According to reconnaissance, there are temporarily no signs of other factions' survival in the surrounding area. Due to the mountain's influence, large tracts of land remain relatively intact. During our arrival in this area, some League garrison forces have already completed the survey and leveling of the land. The League can deploy personnel to resume production activities at any time.

Our main force has reached **Kansk**. According to the survey, the infrastructure in this area is severely damaged, and a large number of factory facilities are completely ruined due to a lack of timely maintenance. Coal mining facilities, being buried deeper, are relatively well-preserved, and we have promptly begun resuming production. Please provide instructions, Generalissimo.

options.name: Prioritize the resumption of industrial production in Kansk to restore the League's energy supply.
Prioritize controlling Kyzyl to ensure the safety of agricultural production.
Kansk and Kyzyl are both crucial; both must proceed simultaneously!

title: Expiation
desc:
Crickets began chirping under the night sky. Moonlight pierced the darkness, casting a glow on Sokolov and the members of his Brotherhood. They had built a bonfire in a square and were sharing the spoils they had plundered that day. It was another fruitful day; they had unexpectedly found some arms and eliminated a few small, uncooperative gangs. The new recruits were a bit reserved; some fiddled with their fingers, others quietly kicked at the dirt underfoot. The gang leaders in the middle of the fire were enjoying themselves. Sokolov grinned, pulled out a rolled cigarette, and lit it up. He tilted his head and shouted.

"Misha! Is the meat ready?"

"Almost, Boss! Bringing it right over!"

He turned and looked at the distant ruins: "How wonderful. How did this small place manage to store so much stuff?"

Suddenly, a few bursts of thunder echoed from the distant night. Sokolov quickly scrambled up as a series of explosions immediately followed the line of the bonfire. The Brotherhood's newcomers started to panic. A cadre, yelling for them to stop, was instantly gunned down. Immediately after, lights from all directions tore through the darkness. A stream of figures in black passed through the night, firing accurately at the disorganized gang members. Sokolov was quickly handcuffed by a man in black. His remaining few subordinates were also captured.

"I knew it. You guys didn't all die off," he said, looking at the familiar Black League soldiers, a bitter smile on his face. "So, the supplies we got were all League caches?"

"Of course. These are all the Generalissimo's orders," the leader in black nodded. "Including the small gangs you eliminated, they were all guided by us. For that, we actually have to thank you for wiping out the minor forces we couldn't locate. Alright, any last words?"
